summary: First checkpoint of the blueprint for Euler systems and the unconditional cyclotomic main conjecture. It decomposes layer L0 from Rubin's Euler systems (Chapter III §2.1–2.4 with the Chapter I–II definitions it uses) and RJW §10.2 and §10.5. The layer contains: the distribution relation for 1 − ζ over any cyclotomic step, with the sign dictionary to Rubin's ζ − 1 form (whose ℓ = 2 case is wrong as printed); the p-extended cyclotomic numbers c̃_m and their real norms, with the tower and auxiliary-prime relations and non-torsion; the comparison with the smoothed units c(a) and the smoothing divisor θ_a; the Kummer classes and the theorem that they form an Euler system for (ℤ_p(1), ℚ^ab, p); χ-components and twisted sums; the χ-cyclotomic generators and units; and Rubin's c_ℚ = ξ_{L,χ}^{1 − χ^{−1}(p)}. The carrier, the tower and the cohomology are imported by six requests. Layers L1–L4 are not yet read. Checkpoint 2 plans L1: Theorem III.2.3 (|A_L^χ| divides [E_L^χ : C_{L,χ}] for p > 2, χ(p) ≠ 1) from Theorem II.2.2, with its hypotheses, vanishing error terms, the index of divisibility and the class-group Selmer group, and Corollary III.2.4 with its dependence on the ψ(p) = 1 components recorded. Checkpoint 3 plans L2: the Iwasawa-theoretic divisibility char(A_∞^χ) | char(E_∞^χ/C_{∞,χ}) (Rubin III.2.7), from Theorem II.3.3, Proposition III.2.6 and the Λ-index, with the augmentation corrections when χ(p) = 1. Checkpoint 4 plans L3: the four-term sequence with the register's corrections, the trivial component, the componentwise equality and the main conjecture for odd p, with the local-unit theorem requested from ColemanPowerSeries L4 and the finite-layer stabilisation recorded as a gap. Checkpoint 5 starts L4 from Greither (Ann. Inst. Fourier 1992): χ-parts for all p, semilocal units modulo circular units, the real main conjecture for all p including 2, Kummer duality, and the main conjecture with the one-half normalisation. Checkpoint 6 plans Greither §4: Theorem B (= 4.1) at p = 2 through the χ(2) ≠ 1 case and the trivial-zero case (Lemma 4.2–Theorem 4.6 with the Gauss-sum computation), Theorem A (the Iwasawa–Leopoldt conjecture at p = 2), Theorems 4.11 and C for real fields, and the Gras conjecture (4.14–4.15). It records eight source issues, E4–E11. E5 is an error in the proof of Theorem 4.6: the Gauss sum lies in the decomposition field of 2, not in F, and its norm to F repairs the proof. E11 is a false sentence in the proof of Lemma 4.13 at p = 2 whose step survives. The rest are misprints. Checkpoint 7 completes L3's formulations. The odd-character form follows from Theorem 13.8 by Kummer duality. The Tate-twisted Greenberg Selmer form (RJW §13.5) is planned for every n: Greenberg's corank statement for all n, and the characteristic ideals in the critical cases (even n ≥ 2 and odd n ≤ −1). For even n this includes the twisted augmentation factor that RJW's Example 13.22 leaves implicit. Two new misprints are recorded, E12 and E13. Checkpoint 8 decomposes Greither §2, the semilocal units and circular units for every p. It covers the norm descent with bounded errors, the circular-unit limit, Coleman's sequences over unramified coefficients including p = 2, one generator per character, and the Stickelberger image of the circular units. Three new misprints are recorded, E14–E16. Checkpoint 9 decomposes the rest of Greither §3: the p = 2 Chebotarev step, the finite-level links, and the inductive Kolyvagin argument proving Theorem 3.1. One new misprint is recorded, E17.

nodes.title: Minimal polynomial of a cyclotomic step when ℓ divides m
nodes.statement: Let ℓ be prime with ℓ ∣ m, K = ℚ(μ_m) ⊆ L = ℚ(μ_{mℓ}), ζ ∈ L a primitive mℓ-th root of unity and η = ζ^ℓ ∈ K. Then the minimal polynomial of ζ over K is X^ℓ − η.
hypotheses: ℓ is prime and m ≥ 1; K and L are cyclotomic over ℚ of conductors m and mℓ (Mathlib's IsCyclotomicExtension {m} ℚ K and {mℓ} ℚ L), with L a K-algebra.
ζ ∈ L is a primitive mℓ-th root of unity and η ∈ K satisfies η = ζ^ℓ in L, so η is a primitive m-th root; this is the compatibility ζ_{mℓ}^ℓ = ζ_m that Rubin fixes before (2).
ℓ ∣ m.
proofSteps: [L : ℚ] = φ(mℓ) = ℓ·φ(m) because ℓ ∣ m (Nat.totient_mul_of_prime_of_dvd), and [K : ℚ] = φ(m); both from IsCyclotomicExtension.finrank with the irreducibility of the rational cyclotomic polynomials.
By the tower law (Module.finrank_mul_finrank), [L : K] = ℓ. L is generated over ℚ, hence over K, by ζ, so deg minpoly_K(ζ) = ℓ (IntermediateField.adjoin.finrank).
ζ is a root of the monic degree-ℓ polynomial X^ℓ − η ∈ K[X], so minpoly_K(ζ) divides it (minpoly.dvd); both are monic of degree ℓ, so they are equal.
acceptance: m = 2, ℓ = 2: the minimal polynomial of i over ℚ is X² + 1 = X² − ζ₂.
m = p^{n−1}, ℓ = p: this is RJW's X^p − ξ_{p^{n−1}} in the proof of Lemma 10.3.

nodes.title: Minimal polynomial of a cyclotomic step when ℓ does not divide m
nodes.statement: Let ℓ be prime with ℓ ∤ m, and let ℓ' satisfy ℓℓ' ≡ 1 (mod m). With K, L, ζ, η as before, η^{ℓ'} ∈ K is a root of X^ℓ − η, and minpoly_K(ζ)·(X − η^{ℓ'}) = X^ℓ − η. So the conjugates of ζ over K are the ℓ-th roots of η other than η^{ℓ'}, the unique one of order dividing m.
hypotheses: ℓ is prime and m ≥ 1; K and L are cyclotomic over ℚ of conductors m and mℓ (Mathlib's IsCyclotomicExtension {m} ℚ K and {mℓ} ℚ L), with L a K-algebra.
ζ ∈ L is a primitive mℓ-th root of unity and η ∈ K satisfies η = ζ^ℓ in L, so η is a primitive m-th root; this is the compatibility ζ_{mℓ}^ℓ = ζ_m that Rubin fixes before (2).
ℓ ∤ m and ℓℓ' ≡ 1 (mod m); for m = 1 every ℓ' works and η = 1.
proofSteps: [L : ℚ] = φ(m)(ℓ − 1) (Nat.totient_mul for coprime m, ℓ, and φ(ℓ) = ℓ − 1), so [L : K] = ℓ − 1 by the tower law.
(η^{ℓ'})^ℓ = η^{ℓℓ'} = η because η^m = 1, so X − η^{ℓ'} divides X^ℓ − η in K[X]; the quotient g is monic of degree ℓ − 1.
ζ ≠ η^{ℓ'} since ζ has order mℓ and η^{ℓ'} has order dividing m, so g(ζ) = 0; hence minpoly_K(ζ) divides g, and equality follows from the degrees.
acceptance: m = 3, ℓ = 2: L = ℚ(μ_6) = K, and minpoly is X − ζ_6 with ζ_6 = −ζ_3² (the other root of X² − ζ_3 is ζ_3², the one of order 3).

nodes.title: Distribution relation, ℓ dividing m
nodes.statement: With K = ℚ(μ_m) ⊆ L = ℚ(μ_{mℓ}), ζ = ζ_{mℓ}, η = ζ^ℓ = ζ_m and ℓ ∣ m: N_{L/K}(1 − ζ) = 1 − η.
hypotheses: ℓ is prime and m ≥ 1; K and L are cyclotomic over ℚ of conductors m and mℓ (Mathlib's IsCyclotomicExtension {m} ℚ K and {mℓ} ℚ L), with L a K-algebra.
ζ ∈ L is a primitive mℓ-th root of unity and η ∈ K satisfies η = ζ^ℓ in L, so η is a primitive m-th root; this is the compatibility ζ_{mℓ}^ℓ = ζ_m that Rubin fixes before (2).
ℓ ∣ m.
The 1 − ζ convention; Rubin's ζ − 1 form differs by (−1)^ℓ (distribution-relation-rubin-convention).
proofSteps: L/K is Galois (cyclotomic), so N_{L/K}(1 − ζ) = ∏_{σ ∈ Gal(L/K)} (1 − σζ) (Algebra.norm_eq_prod_automorphisms).
The σζ are the roots of minpoly_K(ζ) = X^ℓ − η, each once, so the product is the value of X^ℓ − η at X = 1, namely 1 − η.

hypotheses: ℓ is prime and m ≥ 1; K and L are cyclotomic over ℚ of conductors m and mℓ (Mathlib's IsCyclotomicExtension {m} ℚ K and {mℓ} ℚ L), with L a K-algebra.

nodes.title: Distribution relation with the arithmetic Frobenius
nodes.statement: Let σ ∈ Gal(ℚ(μ_m)/ℚ) be the inverse of the arithmetic Frobenius Fr_ℓ (ζ_m ↦ ζ_m^ℓ), that is the image of ℓ^{−1} ∈ (ℤ/m)^× under Mathlib's autEquivPow. For ℓ ∤ m, N_{ℚ(μ_{mℓ})/ℚ(μ_m)}(1 − ζ_{mℓ})·σ(1 − ζ_m) = 1 − ζ_m.
hypotheses: ℓ is prime and m ≥ 1; K and L are cyclotomic over ℚ of conductors m and mℓ (Mathlib's IsCyclotomicExtension {m} ℚ K and {mℓ} ℚ L), with L a K-algebra.
ζ ∈ L is a primitive mℓ-th root of unity and η ∈ K satisfies η = ζ^ℓ in L, so η is a primitive m-th root; this is the compatibility ζ_{mℓ}^ℓ = ζ_m that Rubin fixes before (2).
ℓ is coprime to m.
proofSteps: σ(ζ_m) = ζ_m^{ℓ'} for any ℓ' ≡ ℓ^{−1} (mod m), by the defining property of autEquivPow.
Substitute into distribution-relation-of-not-dvd.
acceptance: Fr_ℓ is the arithmetic Frobenius, as in Rubin and in RJW Definition 10.16 (σ_ℓ the image of Frob_ℓ); the Euler factor involves Fr_ℓ^{−1}.

nodes.title: The ζ − 1 convention and its sign
nodes.statement: For any finite field extension L/K and ζ ∈ L, N_{L/K}(ζ − 1) = (−1)^{[L:K]} N_{L/K}(1 − ζ). Hence, for the cyclotomic step, N(ζ_{mℓ} − 1) = (−1)^{ℓ+1}(ζ_m − 1) if ℓ ∣ m and N(ζ_{mℓ} − 1) = (−1)^{ℓ−1}(ζ_m − 1)^{1 − Fr_ℓ^{−1}} if ℓ ∤ m, m > 1. For odd ℓ these are Rubin's formulas (2); for ℓ = 2 his first two cases need the sign −1.
hypotheses: [L : K] = ℓ when ℓ ∣ m and ℓ − 1 when ℓ ∤ m (the two minimal-polynomial nodes).
proofSteps: N is multiplicative and N_{L/K}(−1) = (−1)^{[L:K]} (the norm of an element of K is its [L:K]-th power, Algebra.norm_algebraMap).
Combine with distribution-relation-of-dvd and distribution-relation-of-not-dvd.
acceptance: Counterexample to the printed (2) at ℓ = 2: N_{ℚ(i)/ℚ}(i − 1) = 2 while ζ_2 − 1 = −2.
Second counterexample: ℓ = 2, m = 3 gives ζ_6 − 1 = ζ_3 while (ζ_3 − 1)^{1 − Fr_2^{−1}} = −ζ_3.

nodes.title: The p-extended cyclotomic numbers c̃_m
nodes.statement: Fix a prime p and the compatible roots ζ_m with the tower ℚ(μ_m) (requested from IntegralIwasawaTheory:L0). For m ≥ 1 put c̃_m = N_{ℚ(μ_{mp})/ℚ(μ_m)}(1 − ζ_{mp}) ∈ ℚ(μ_m)^×. This is Rubin's c̃_{m∞} in the 1 − ζ convention: Rubin's element N(ζ_{mp} − 1) equals (−1)^{[ℚ(μ_{mp}):ℚ(μ_m)]}c̃_m.
hypotheses: p prime; m ≥ 1. No coprimality between m and p is assumed.
The extra norm from level mp is what makes the family norm-compatible in the p-direction (Rubin, Remark 2.1); it loses information when p ∤ m.
proofSteps: Definition as a relative norm.

nodes.title: Auxiliary-prime relation for c̃
nodes.statement: For a prime ℓ ≠ p and m ≥ 1: N_{ℚ(μ_{mℓ})/ℚ(μ_m)}(c̃_{mℓ}) = c̃_m^{1 − Fr_ℓ^{−1}} if ℓ ∤ m, and = c̃_m if ℓ ∣ m. Here Fr_ℓ ∈ Gal(ℚ(μ_m)/ℚ). The case m = 1 is included (then Fr_ℓ = 1 and the norm is 1).
hypotheses: ℓ prime, ℓ ≠ p; m ≥ 1.
The conductor-one exception of (2) never occurs, because c̃ is a norm from level mp > 1.
proofSteps: Norms are transitive in the square ℚ(μ_m) ⊆ ℚ(μ_{mp}), ℚ(μ_{mℓ}) ⊆ ℚ(μ_{mℓp}) (Algebra.norm_norm), so the left side is N_{ℚ(μ_{mp})/ℚ(μ_m)}(N_{ℚ(μ_{mℓp})/ℚ(μ_{mp})}(1 − ζ_{mℓp})).
Apply distribution-relation-of-dvd (ℓ ∣ mp) or distribution-relation-frobenius (ℓ ∤ mp) at level mp.
The norm N_{ℚ(μ_{mp})/ℚ(μ_m)} commutes with the Galois action (the extensions are abelian), and Fr_ℓ on ℚ(μ_{mp}) restricts to Fr_ℓ on ℚ(μ_m) (IntegralIwasawaTheory:L0).
acceptance: Checked numerically for p ∈ {2, 3, 5, 7}, m < 30 and ℓ ≤ 13: 812 cases, no failure, including p = 2 and ℓ = 2.

hypotheses: m ≥ 1; ℓ ≠ p prime.

nodes.title: Smoothed cyclotomic units and the smoothing divisor
nodes.statement: Let m ≥ 2 and a ∈ ℕ coprime to m. Then c_m(a) = (1 − ζ_m^a)/(1 − ζ_m) = ∑_{i<a} ζ_m^i is a unit of ℤ[ζ_m] and equals σ_a(1 − ζ_m)/(1 − ζ_m). If p ∣ m it equals σ_a(c̃_m)/c̃_m = c̃_m^{σ_a − 1}; for m = p^n it is RJW's c_n(a) = (ξ^a − 1)/(ξ − 1). The operator σ_a − 1 is the image of the smoothing divisor θ_a = δ_a − δ_1 (the denominator of DirichletPadicLFunctions:L1/arithmetic-pseudomeasure) under the finite projection Λ(ℤ_p^×) → ℤ_p[(ℤ/p^n)^×] ≅ ℤ_p[Gal(ℚ(μ_{p^n})/ℚ)], δ_u ↦ σ_{u mod p^n}. The smoothed family {c̃_m^{σ_a − 1} : (m, a) = 1} satisfies the relations of p-extended-tower-relation and p-extended-auxiliary-relation for the primes ℓ ∤ a.
hypotheses: m ≥ 2 and gcd(a, m) = 1; a need not be prime to p for the unit statement, but the family indexed by all m requires the primes dividing a to be excluded, since σ_a is defined only on ℚ(μ_m) with (a, m) = 1.
a = ±1 gives the torsion elements 1 and −ζ_m^{−1}; the nondegenerate smoothing uses a ∉ {0, ±1}.
proofSteps: The quotient is the geometric sum, a unit by IsPrimitiveRoot.geom_sum_isUnit.
σ_a(1 − ζ_m) = 1 − ζ_m^a by definition of σ_a (IntegralIwasawaTheory:L0); for p ∣ m use pCycNumber_of_dvd.

Under the finite projection (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L1/finite-projection-algebra-map) with the Dirac homomorphism (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L1/dirac-hom) and unit reduction (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L1/unit-reduction), δ_a − δ_1 maps to [a mod p^n] − [1], which acts as σ_a − 1.
σ_a commutes with the relative norms, so the relations transfer.
acceptance: The signs of the ζ − 1 and 1 − ζ conventions cancel in the quotient.

nodes.title: ℚ^ab and N = p satisfy the Euler-system hypotheses
nodes.statement: The pair (𝒦, N) = (ℚ^ab, p) satisfies Rubin's Definition II.1.1: (i) 𝒦 contains ℚ(q) for every prime q ≠ p; (ii) 𝒦 contains the cyclotomic ℤ_p-extension ℚ_∞, in which no finite prime splits completely. In the conductor-indexed presentation of Remark II.1.3, the fields are 𝒦 ∩ ℚ[m∞] = ℚ(μ_m) and 𝒦 ∩ ℚ[m] = ℚ(μ_m)^+.
hypotheses: p prime (Rubin's §2.1 takes any p; the applications take p > 2).
proofSteps: (i) ℚ(q) lies in the ray class field modulo q, which is ℚ(μ_q)^+ ⊆ ℚ^ab (class field theory over ℚ).

(ii) ℚ_∞ ⊆ ℚ(μ_{p^∞}) ⊆ ℚ^ab with Gal(ℚ_∞/ℚ) ≅ ℤ_p; p is totally ramified, and for q ≠ p the Frobenius of q has image q in ℤ_p^×, which is not a root of unity, so its image in ℤ_p has infinite order and the decomposition group is infinite (Rubin, Remark II.1.2).
The ray class fields of ℚ modulo m∞ and m are ℚ(μ_m) and ℚ(μ_m)^+.
acceptance: Every hypothesis of Definition II.1.1 is checked for this 𝒦 and N, not assumed.

nodes.title: Kummer classes of the cyclotomic numbers
nodes.statement: For N ≥ 0 and m ≥ 1, κ_N(c̃_m) ∈ H¹(G_{ℚ(μ_m)}, μ_{p^N}) is the Tau Ceti Kummer class of c̃_m (TauCeti.kummerMap, n = p^N invertible in characteristic 0), and likewise κ_N(c̃_m^+) over ℚ(μ_m)^+. The classes are compatible in N, and define κ(c̃_m) ∈ H¹(ℚ(μ_m), ℤ_p(1)) = lim_N H¹(ℚ(μ_m), μ_{p^N}) = (ℚ(μ_m)^×)^, Rubin's (1).
hypotheses: p prime; p^N is invertible in every number field.
The inverse limit and the identification with the p-adic completion are requested from SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L0.
proofSteps: Apply TauCeti.kummerMap to c̃_m and c̃_m^+.
Compatibility in N: the p-th power map μ_{p^{N+1}} → μ_{p^N} commutes with the Kummer maps (connecting maps of compatible Kummer sequences; SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L0).
Norm compatibility: Cor ∘ κ = κ ∘ N (ProfiniteCohomology Layer 9, kummerIso_norm).
acceptance: κ_1(c̃_1) = κ_1(p) ≠ 0 in H¹(G_ℚ, μ_p), as p is not a p-th power in ℚ (TauCeti.kummerMap_eq_one_iff).
For p = 5, κ_N(c̃_3) = κ_N(−ζ_3) = 0: −ζ_3 has order 6, prime to 5, so it is a 5^N-th power.

nodes.title: χ-components
nodes.statement: Let O be a commutative ring, Δ a finite group, M an O[Δ]-module and χ : Δ → O^× a character. The χ-component is M^χ = {x ∈ M : δx = χ(δ)x for all δ ∈ Δ}, an O-submodule. For a ℤ[Δ]-module B, Rubin's B^χ is (B̂ ⊗_{ℤ_p} O)^χ, with B̂ the p-adic completion (B ⊗ ℤ_p for B finitely generated). Equivalently B^χ ≅ (B̂ ⊗ O_{χ^{−1}})^Δ after fixing a generator of O_{χ^{−1}}.
hypotheses: For exactness and the decomposition B̂ ⊗ O = ⊕_χ B^χ, |Δ| must be invertible in O (Rubin: [L : K] prime to p) and O must contain the values of all characters.
When p divides |Δ| the character functors are those of layer L4 (Greither); this node is the prime-to-p case.
proofSteps: Definition as an eigen-submodule; closure under 0, + and O-scalars uses only that O is commutative.
The twist description is Mathlib's invariants (Representation.invariants) of ρ ⊗ χ^{−1}.
Exactness and the decomposition use the idempotents |Δ|^{−1}∑ χ(δ)^{−1}δ (chi-sum), as for Representation.averageMap.
acceptance: The trivial character gives the invariants.

nodes.title: The χ-cyclotomic generators ξ_{n,χ}
nodes.statement: Let χ be an even nontrivial character of G_ℚ of finite order prime to p, with conductor f, fixed field L and Δ = Gal(L/ℚ); let ℚ_n ⊆ ℚ(μ_{p^{n+1}}) be the layers of ℚ_∞ and L_n = Lℚ_n, so Gal(L_n/ℚ_n) = Δ. Put u_0 = N_{ℚ(μ_f)/L}(1 − ζ_f) and, for n > 0, u_n = N_{ℚ(μ_{fp^{n+1}})/L_n}(1 − ζ_{fp^{n+1}}). Then ξ_{n,χ} = chiSum_χ(1 ⊗ u_n) ∈ (O ⊗ L_n^×)^χ. It equals Rubin's ∏_{δ∈Gal(ℚ(μ_f)/ℚ)} (ζ_f^δ − 1)^{χ^{−1}(δ)} (n = 0), respectively the product over Gal(ℚ_n(μ_{fp^{n+1}})/ℚ_n) (n > 0).
hypotheses: χ even, nontrivial, of order prime to p (Rubin §III.2.2); χ is viewed as a Dirichlet character modulo f with χ(q) = 0 for q ∣ f.
The sign convention is immaterial: ∑ χ^{−1}(δ) = 0 over each group, since χ is nontrivial on it, so (−1) contributes (−1)^0.
proofSteps: Rewrite Rubin's product over Gal(ℚ(μ_f)/ℚ) by grouping δ by its restriction to L: χ^{−1}(δ) depends only on δ|_L, and the inner product is the norm to L. This keeps ξ in L_n^× ⊗ O without a descent step (p may divide [ℚ(μ_f) : L]).
chiSum lands in the χ-component (chiSum_mem).
acceptance: For χ the quadratic character of conductor 5 and p = 3: L = ℚ(√5), u_0 = (1 − ζ_5)(1 − ζ_5^{−1}) = (5 − √5)/2 and ξ_{L,χ} = u_0/σ(u_0) = (3 − √5)/2 = ε^{−2}, with ε = (1 + √5)/2.

nodes.title: The twisted class c_ℚ
nodes.statement: Let c = c̃^{χ^{−1}} be the twist by χ^{−1} of the Euler system of cyclotomic units (ES.2, Rubin Proposition II.4.2), an Euler system for (T^*, ℚ^ab, pf) with T = O_χ, T^* = ℤ_p(1) ⊗ χ^{−1}. Under the restriction–Kummer isomorphism H¹(ℚ, T^*) ≅ (L^×)^χ ⊆ L^× ⊗̂ O (Rubin (3)), c_ℚ corresponds to chiSum_χ(1 ⊗ N_{ℚ(μ_{fp})/L}(1 − ζ_{fp})) = ∏_{δ∈Gal(ℚ(μ_{fp})/ℚ)} (1 − ζ_{fp}^δ)^{χ^{−1}(δ)}.
hypotheses: χ even, nontrivial, of order prime to p, conductor f; [L : ℚ] prime to p.
proofSteps: ES.2's twisting lemma (Rubin Lemma II.4.3) with F = ℚ and L' = ℚ(μ_f)^+, which has the same conductor as L because χ is even, gives ∏_{δ∈Gal(ℚ(μ_f)^+/ℚ)} (δc̃_f^+)^{χ^{−1}(δ)}.
c̃_f^+ = N_{ℚ(μ_f)/ℚ(μ_f)^+}N_{ℚ(μ_{fp})/ℚ(μ_f)}(1 − ζ_{fp}), so the product is the one over Gal(ℚ(μ_{fp})/ℚ); the sign convention is immaterial for χ ≠ 1.
acceptance: For p ∣ f the norm N_{ℚ(μ_{fp})/ℚ(μ_f)}(1 − ζ_{fp}) is 1 − ζ_f.

nodes.title: c_ℚ = ξ_{L,χ}^{1 − χ^{−1}(p)}
nodes.statement: With χ as above and χ(p) = 0 when p ∣ f: c_ℚ = ξ_{L,χ}^{1 − χ^{−1}(p)} in (L^×)^χ, that is chiSum_χ(1 ⊗ N_{ℚ(μ_{fp})/L}(1 − ζ_{fp})) = (1 − χ^{−1}(p))·ξ_{L,χ}.
hypotheses: χ even, nontrivial, of order prime to p, conductor f.
proofSteps: By twisted-class-formula, c_ℚ is chiSum_χ(1 ⊗ u') with u' = N_{ℚ(μ_f)/L}(N_{ℚ(μ_{fp})/ℚ(μ_f)}(1 − ζ_{fp})).

If p ∤ f, the inner norm is (1 − ζ_f)^{1 − Fr_p^{−1}} (distribution-relation-frobenius), so u' = u_0 − Fr_p^{−1}u_0 additively; chi-sum-frobenius with φ = Fr_p|_L gives (1 − χ(Fr_p)^{−1})ξ_{L,χ} = (1 − χ^{−1}(p))ξ_{L,χ}.
If p ∣ f, the inner norm is 1 − ζ_f (distribution-relation-of-dvd), so c_ℚ = ξ_{L,χ} = ξ_{L,χ}^{1 − 0}.
acceptance: For χ(p) = 1 the class c_ℚ is trivial: this is the source of Rubin's hypothesis χ(p) ≠ 1 (Remark III.2.1).

nodes.title: Hypotheses of Theorem II.2.2 and vanishing of its error terms for the cyclotomic twist
nodes.statement: Let p > 2 and χ : G_ℚ → O^× even, nontrivial, of finite order prime to p, with conductor f and field L; T = O_χ, W = D_χ, T* = O_{χ^{−1}}(1), W* = T* ⊗ ℚ_p/ℤ_p. Then T* satisfies Hyp(ℚ, T*) with τ = 1, because rank_O T* = 1 (Remark II.2.4). For the Euler system c = c̃^{χ^{−1}} for (T*, ℚ^ab, pf), the field Ω of Theorem II.2.2 is L(μ_{p^∞}). Both error terms n_{W*} and n*_{W*} of Theorem II.2.2 vanish: H¹(Ω/ℚ, W) = 0 because χ ≠ 1 (Lemma III.1.1(i)), and H¹(Ω/ℚ, W*) = 0 because χ is even, so it is not congruent modulo p to the odd cyclotomic character (Lemma III.1.1(ii)).
hypotheses: Theorem II.2.2 is applied to T* in place of T. Its bound is then on S_{Σ_p}(ℚ, W), the dual of W* being W.
Over ℚ, K(1) = ℚ and (O_ℚ^×)^{1/p^∞} ⊂ ℚ(μ_{p^∞}), since ±1 are p-th powers for odd p. So Ω = ℚ(W*)ℚ(μ_{p^∞}) = L(μ_{p^∞}).
proofSteps: Rank one gives Hyp(ℚ, T*)(i) with τ = 1 and (ii) trivially (Remark II.2.4).

Lemma III.1.1: since |Δ| is prime to p, inflation–restriction gives H¹(Ω/ℚ, k_ρ) = Hom(Gal(Ω/L), k_ρ^Δ). This vanishes if ρ ≢ 1 mod p, and then H¹(Ω/ℚ, D_ρ) = 0 by dévissage. Take ρ = χ, and ρ = χ^{−1}ε_cyc, which is odd while χ is even, so ρ ≢ 1 for p > 2.
acceptance: χ = 1 is excluded: then H¹(Ω/ℚ, W) ≠ 0 in general.
An odd χ can be congruent to ε_cyc (for instance χ = ω), which is why χ is even here.

nodes.title: E_L^χ is free of rank one, and the index of divisibility is the unit index
nodes.statement: Let p > 2 and χ : G_ℚ → O^× even, nontrivial, of finite order prime to p, with conductor f and field L; T = O_χ, W = D_χ, T* = O_{χ^{−1}}(1), W* = T* ⊗ ℚ_p/ℤ_p, with χ(p) ≠ 1. Then E_L^χ is a free O-module of rank one, by the Dirichlet unit theorem, since L is totally real and χ ≠ 1 is even. The index of divisibility of the cyclotomic Euler system (Definition II.2.1) is ind_O(c) = ℓ_O(E_L^χ/C_{L,χ}). Indeed L^×/E_L is torsion-free, so a generator of C_{L,χ} is divisible by p^n in H¹(ℚ, T*) ≅ (L^×)^χ exactly when it is divisible by p^n in E_L^χ.
hypotheses: The Galois-module form of the unit theorem is needed: E_L ⊗ ℚ is the augmentation quotient of ℚ[Δ] for totally real L (Herbrand–Minkowski). This is requested with IntegralIwasawaTheory L0. Mathlib has the rank statement (NumberField.Units.finrank_eq) but not the Δ-module structure.
c_ℚ generates C_{L,χ} when χ(p) ≠ 1 (L0/twisted-class-generates).
proofSteps: The χ-part of μ(L) ⊗ ℤ_p vanishes for odd p, so E_L^χ is torsion-free.
E_L ⊗ ℚ_p ≅ (augmentation quotient of ℚ_p[Δ]) contains each nontrivial character once. So E_L^χ has O-rank one, and it is free, being torsion-free over a DVR.
H¹(ℚ, T*) ≅ (L^×)^χ by (3). Since L^×/E_L is torsion-free, divisibility of c_ℚ in H¹/torsion is divisibility in E_L^χ. With c_ℚ a generator of C_{L,χ}, ind_O(c) = ℓ_O(E_L^χ/C_{L,χ}).
acceptance: If χ(p) = 1 then c_ℚ = 0 and ind_O(c) = ∞ (Remark II.2.8).

nodes.title: When χ(p) ≠ 1 the relaxed Selmer group is Hom_O(A_L^χ, D)
nodes.statement: Let χ : G_ℚ → O^× even, nontrivial, of finite order prime to p, with conductor f and field L; T = O_χ, W = D_χ, T* = O_{χ^{−1}}(1), W* = T* ⊗ ℚ_p/ℤ_p, with χ(p) ≠ 1. Then H¹_f(ℚ_p, W) = 0, so S_{Σ_p}(ℚ, W) = S(ℚ, W) ≅ Hom_O(A_L^χ, D), where A_L is the ideal class group of L.

So H¹_f(ℚ_p, W) = 0 and relaxing the condition at p changes nothing: S_{Σ_p}(ℚ, W) = S(ℚ, W).

nodes.title: The limit of units, local units and cyclotomic units (Rubin, Proposition III.2.6)
nodes.statement: Let p an odd prime and χ : G_ℚ → O^× even, nontrivial, of finite order prime to p, with field L, Λ = O[[Gal(ℚ_∞/ℚ)]] and J = char(O) its augmentation ideal. With A_∞, E_∞, C_{∞,χ}, U_∞, Y_∞ = lim (L_{n,p})^ and E′_∞ = lim (E′_n)^ (p-units) the norm inverse limits: (i) the restriction isomorphisms identify Λ{c_{ℚ_n}} ⊂ H¹_∞(ℚ, T*) ⊂ H¹_∞(ℚ_p, T*) ↠ H¹_{∞,s}(ℚ_p, T*) with C_{∞,χ} ⊂ (E′_∞)^χ ⊂ Y_∞^χ ↠ Y_∞^χ/U_∞^χ; (ii) Y_∞^χ/U_∞^χ ≅ ℤ_p[Δ/Δ_p]^χ, which is 0 if χ(p) ≠ 1 and O if χ(p) = 1; (iii) (E′_∞)^χ/E_∞^χ injects into O.

H¹_∞(ℚ, T*) = lim S^{p}(ℚ_n, T*) is Rubin's Corollary B.3.4, requested with SelmerIwasawaCohomology L3.

S^{p}(ℚ_n, T*) ≅ (E′_n)^χ by (3), and the local restriction isomorphisms H¹(ℚ_{n,p}, T*) ≅ (L_{n,p}^×)^χ ⊃ H¹_f ≅ U_n^χ give the rest.
(ii): L_{m,p}^×/U_m ≅ ⊕_{w|p} ℤ ≅ ℤ[Δ/Δ_p] compatibly with norms, and ℤ_p[Δ/Δ_p]^χ ≠ 0 exactly when χ is trivial on Δ_p, that is χ(p) = 1.
(iii): E_∞^χ is the kernel of (E′_∞)^χ → Y_∞^χ/U_∞^χ.

nodes.statement: Let p an odd prime and χ : G_ℚ → O^× even, nontrivial, of finite order prime to p, with field L, Λ = O[[Gal(ℚ_∞/ℚ)]] and J = char(O) its augmentation ideal. Then (E′_∞)^χ is a torsion-free, finitely generated Λ-module of rank one, ind_Λ(c) = char((E′_∞)^χ/C_{∞,χ}), and ind_Λ(c) divides J·char(E_∞^χ/C_{∞,χ}).

Proposition III.2.6(i) identifies c_{ℚ,∞} with a generator of C_{∞,χ} inside (E′_∞)^χ ≅ H¹_∞(ℚ, T*). So ind_Λ(c) = {φ(c) : φ ∈ Hom_Λ(H¹_∞, Λ)} = char((E′_∞)^χ/C_{∞,χ}).
By Proposition III.2.6(iii), char((E′_∞)^χ/E_∞^χ) divides char(O) = J, and multiplicativity of char gives the divisibility.

nodes.statement: Let p an odd prime and χ : G_ℚ → O^× even, nontrivial, of finite order prime to p, with field L, Λ = O[[Gal(ℚ_∞/ℚ)]] and J = char(O) its augmentation ideal. Then char(A_∞^χ) divides char(E_∞^χ/C_{∞,χ}), where A_∞ = lim A_n is the inverse limit of the p-parts of the class groups of L_n. No hypothesis on χ(p) is needed.
hypotheses: Theorem II.3.3 and Proposition II.3.7 are imported (ES.8). Hom_O(S(ℚ_∞, W), D) ≅ A_∞^χ is (5).
Leopoldt's conjecture for the real abelian field L is used to exclude J from char(A_∞^χ).
proofSteps: Theorem II.3.3 with Proposition II.3.7: char(Hom_O(S(ℚ_∞, W), D)) divides ind_Λ(c)·char(H¹_{∞,s}(ℚ_p, T*)).

ind_Λ(c) divides J·char(E_∞^χ/C_{∞,χ}) (L2/lambda-index-of-cyclotomic-units), and char(H¹_{∞,s}(ℚ_p, T*)) = char(Y_∞^χ/U_∞^χ) divides J (Proposition III.2.6(ii)). So char(A_∞^χ) divides J²·char(E_∞^χ/C_{∞,χ}).

J does not divide char(A_∞^χ). J | char(A_∞^χ) iff A_∞^χ/JA_∞^χ = Gal(M_∞/L_∞)^χ is infinite, with M_∞/L abelian. L is real abelian, so Leopoldt holds and L has no ℤ_p²-extension. So Gal(M_∞/L) has ℤ_p-rank one and [M_∞ : L_∞] is finite ([Iw3] §3.1).
Since J is a height-one prime of the UFD Λ, coprime to char(A_∞^χ), the J² can be removed.
acceptance: χ(p) ≠ 1: the J-terms are units and step 3 is not needed.
χ(p) = 1: both J-factors are present and step 3 removes them. This is the augmentation correction the roadmap asks for.

nodes.title: The four-term sequence 0 → E⁺/C⁺ → U⁺/C⁺ → X⁺ → Y⁺ → 0 (RJW 13.13–13.14, corrected)
nodes.statement: Let p an odd prime, F_n = ℚ(μ_{p^n}), F_∞^+ = ∪F_n^+, G^+ = Γ^+ = Gal(F_∞^+/ℚ), Λ = Λ(Γ^+), and U^+_{∞,1}, E^+_{∞,1}, C^+_{∞,1} the limits of the principal local units, the closures of the global units and of the cyclotomic units in them (RJW Definitions 11.8, 13.12). Let X_∞^+ = Gal(M_∞^+/F_∞^+) and Y_∞^+ = Gal(L_∞^+/F_∞^+), where M_∞^+ (resp. L_∞^+) is the maximal abelian pro-p extension of F_∞^+ unramified outside p (resp. unramified). Then there is an exact sequence of Λ-modules 0 → E^+_{∞,1} → U^+_{∞,1} → Gal(M_∞^+/L_∞^+) → 0 (Proposition 13.13). Hence Gal(M_∞^+/L_∞^+) ≅ U^+_{∞,1}/E^+_{∞,1} ≅ (U^+_{∞,1}/C^+_{∞,1})/(E^+_{∞,1}/C^+_{∞,1}), and 0 → E^+_{∞,1}/C^+_{∞,1} → U^+_{∞,1}/C^+_{∞,1} → X_∞^+ → Y_∞^+ → 0 is exact (Corollary 13.14).
hypotheses: RJW's proof prints Gal(M_∞^+/L_∞^+) ≅ E/U ≅ (E/C)/(U/C); the quotients must be reversed, to U/E ≅ (U/C)/(E/C) (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras/E5). The stated sequence of Corollary 13.14 is unaffected.

RJW justify exactness of the inverse limit by 'finitely generated ℤ_p-modules (so satisfy the Mittag-Leffler condition)'. That implication is false in general (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras/E6: ℤ_p with multiplication by p). The repair used here is compactness: the finite-level modules are compact Hausdorff and the transition maps are continuous, so lim is exact.
E_n → U_n is injective by Leopoldt's conjecture for F_n^+, known by Brumer (RJW's printed rank r₁ + r₂ − 1 = p^{n−1}(p − 1)/2 should read p^{n−1}(p − 1)/2 − 1: PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras/E7).
The finite-level sequence 0 → E^+_{n,1} → U^+_{n,1} → Gal(M_n^+/L_n^+) → 0 is global class field theory (Washington, Corollary 13.6), requested with the Tau Ceti ClassFieldTheory layer.
proofSteps: Class field theory at level n: the Artin map identifies Gal(M_n^+/L_n^+) with U^+_{n,1} modulo the closure of the global units. The kernel is E^+_{n,1}, by Leopoldt.
Pass to the limit over n. The modules are compact and the transitions continuous, so the limit of the short exact sequences is exact (the E6 repair).
Galois theory gives 0 → Gal(M_∞^+/L_∞^+) → X_∞^+ → Y_∞^+ → 0. With C ⊆ E ⊆ U, the first and third isomorphism theorems give U/E ≅ (U/C)/(E/C), which yields the four-term sequence.
acceptance: The orientation check: the printed E/U is not a quotient, since E ⊆ U.

nodes.title: The trivial-character component of the main conjecture
nodes.statement: Let p an odd prime, F_n = ℚ(μ_{p^n}), F_∞^+ = ∪F_n^+, G^+ = Γ^+ = Gal(F_∞^+/ℚ), Λ = Λ(Γ^+), and U^+_{∞,1}, E^+_{∞,1}, C^+_{∞,1} the limits of the principal local units, the closures of the global units and of the cyclotomic units in them (RJW Definitions 11.8, 13.12), and let e₁ be the idempotent of the trivial character of Δ^+ = Gal(ℚ(μ_p)^+/ℚ), so e₁Λ = ℤ_p[[Γ₀]] with Γ₀ ≅ ℤ_p. Then e₁X_∞^+ = e₁Y_∞^+ = 0, and e₁(I(Γ^+)ζ_p) = e₁Λ. So both sides of the main conjecture have trivial component the unit ideal. The pole of ζ_p at the trivial character is cancelled by the augmentation ideal: for a topological generator a of ℤ_p^×, the value of ([a] − [1])ζ_p at the trivial character is −(1 − p^{−1})·log_p(a), a p-adic unit.
hypotheses: ζ_{p,p−1} has a simple pole at s = 1 with residue (1 − p^{−1}) (RJW Theorem 7.1(ii)), and lim_{s→1}(s − 1)^{−1}(⟨a⟩^{1−s} − 1) = −log_p(a) (Lemma 7.2(ii)).
log_p(a) has valuation exactly 1 when a generates ℤ_p^× (p odd), so (1 − p^{−1})log_p(a) ∈ ℤ_p^×.
proofSteps: e₁X_∞^+ is the Galois group over ℚ_∞ of the maximal abelian pro-p extension of ℚ_∞ unramified outside p. Its Γ₀-coinvariants form the Galois group of the maximal abelian pro-p extension of ℚ unramified outside p over ℚ_∞, which is trivial by Kronecker–Weber for odd p. By Nakayama, e₁X_∞^+ = 0, and so its quotient e₁Y_∞^+ = 0.

The value of ([a] − [1])ζ_p at the trivial character is the numerator of (7.1) at s = 1, namely the residue (1 − p^{−1}) times −log_p(a). This is a unit, so ([a] − [1])ζ_p is a unit of the local ring e₁Λ, and e₁(I(Γ^+)ζ_p) = e₁Λ.
acceptance: e₁ζ_p itself is not in e₁Λ (it has a pole); only I(Γ^+)ζ_p is an ideal of Λ (RJW Proposition 11.5).
With e₁X_∞^+ = e₁Y_∞^+ = 0, the four-term sequence gives e₁(E/C) ≅ e₁(U/C) ≅ e₁Λ/e₁(I(Γ^+)ζ_p) = 0.

nodes.title: Equality of characteristic ideals: char(Y_∞^χ) = char(E_∞^χ/C_{∞,χ}) (Rubin, Corollary III.2.8)
nodes.statement: Let p be odd and χ an even nontrivial character of order prime to p, with field L. Then char(A_∞^χ) = char(E_∞^χ/C_{∞,χ}). For L = ℚ(μ_p)^+ and all even χ ≠ 1 of Δ^+ at once, char(Y_∞^+) = char(E^+_{∞,1}/C^+_{∞,1}) away from the trivial component; the trivial components vanish on both sides (L3/trivial-character-component).
hypotheses: Rubin's proof is one line: it cites [MW] §1.6 and [Ru3] p. 414 (Lang's Cyclotomic Fields, appendix), which are not read. See the L3 gap.

The roadmap requires the product-over-characters calculation, coefficient valuations and finite-layer error terms with their stabilisation. The finite-layer input is the class number formula [E_n^+ : C_n^+] = h_n^+ for ℚ(μ_{p^n})^+ (Washington Theorem 8.2), requested from IntegralIwasawaTheory.
proofSteps: For every even χ ≠ 1 of Δ^+, char(Y_∞^χ) divides char(E_∞^χ/C_{∞,χ}) (L2/cyclotomic-iwasawa-divisibility). Here χ(p) = 0, since p divides the conductor.

Take the product over χ. The p-parts of h_n^+ and [E_n^+ : C_n^+] agree at every layer. By Iwasawa's control theorem for Y (Y_n = (Y_∞)_{Γ_n} up to bounded error, p totally ramified) and the corresponding control for E/C, the Iwasawa invariants of ∏_χ char(Y_∞^χ) and ∏_χ char(E_∞^χ/C_{∞,χ}) agree. So the two products are equal.
Equality of the product together with the divisibility of each factor gives equality of each factor. This is the step the roadmap flags: total cardinalities alone would not suffice.
acceptance: A component-by-component equality does not follow from the totals without step 1's divisibilities.

nodes.title: The Iwasawa main conjecture over ℚ for odd p (RJW Theorem 13.8; Rubin Theorem III.2.10)
nodes.statement: Let p an odd prime, F_n = ℚ(μ_{p^n}), F_∞^+ = ∪F_n^+, G^+ = Γ^+ = Gal(F_∞^+/ℚ), Λ = Λ(Γ^+), and U^+_{∞,1}, E^+_{∞,1}, C^+_{∞,1} the limits of the principal local units, the closures of the global units and of the cyclotomic units in them (RJW Definitions 11.8, 13.12). Then X_∞^+ is a finitely generated torsion Λ(Γ^+)-module and char_{Λ(Γ^+)}(X_∞^+) = I(Γ^+)ζ_p (RJW Theorem 13.8). In χ-components: for even χ ≠ 1 of order prime to p, char(Z_∞^χ) = L_χΛ, where Z_∞ is the Galois group of the maximal abelian p-extension of L_∞ unramified outside p (Rubin Theorem III.2.10). This holds for every odd p, unconditionally. The stronger statement X_∞^+ ≅ Λ(Γ^+)/I(Γ^+)ζ_p (RJW Theorem 13.11) is not asserted; it needs p to be a Vandiver prime.
hypotheses: The local-unit theorem U^+_{∞,1}/C^+_{∞,1} ≅ Λ(Γ^+)/I(Γ^+)ζ_p through the Coleman map (RJW Theorem 12.23(ii), Iwasawa) is requested from ColemanPowerSeries L4.
Y_∞^+ is finitely generated and torsion (Iwasawa), requested with IntegralIwasawaTheory.
proofSteps: Take characteristic ideals in the four-term sequence (L3/galois-unit-four-term-sequence). char is multiplicative (RJW Lemma 13.6), so char(E/C)·char(X_∞^+) = char(U/C)·char(Y_∞^+).
char(U/C) = I(Γ^+)ζ_p (Theorem 12.23(ii)), and char(E/C) = char(Y_∞^+) (L3/componentwise-iwasawa-equality), which is nonzero since Y_∞^+ is torsion. Cancel in the domain components of Λ.
Torsion: U/C ≅ Λ/I(Γ^+)ζ_p is torsion because ζ_p ≠ 0, and Y_∞^+ is torsion, so X_∞^+ is torsion. The trivial component is handled by L3/trivial-character-component.
χ-form: the sequence 0 → E_∞^χ/C_{∞,χ} → U_∞^χ/C_{∞,χ} → Z_∞^χ → A_∞^χ → 0 with Corollary III.2.8 and char(U_∞^χ/C_{∞,χ}) = L_χΛ (Theorem III.2.9(ii)) gives Theorem III.2.10.
acceptance: Without the Vandiver hypothesis only characteristic ideals are compared, not modules.
p = 2 is not covered here (Greither, L4).

nodes.title: Greither's χ-parts, including the case p ∣ |Δ|
nodes.statement: Let Δ be a finite abelian group, χ a p-adic character of Δ, and M a ℤ_p[Δ]-module. The χ-part of M is M_χ = M ⊗_{ℤ_p[Δ]} ℤ_p(χ), where ℤ_p(χ) = ℤ_p[χ(δ) | δ ∈ Δ] with Δ acting through χ. Properties: (a) M ↦ M_χ is right exact, and exact if p ∤ |Δ|; (b) Q_p-conjugate characters give isomorphic parts; (c) the kernels of ℤ_p[Δ] → ℤ_p(χ) are the minimal primes of ℤ_p[Δ]; (d) if p ∤ |Δ|, M ≅ ∏_χ M_χ over Q_p-conjugacy classes. For Δ = Gal(F/ℚ) with complex conjugation j: (e) for odd χ, (1 + j)M maps to 0 in M_χ; (f) for M = A_p(F), M_χ ≅ (M/im M^+)_χ for odd χ; (g) if p = 2 and Δ = Δ₂ × Δ₀ with Δ₀ odd and Δ₂ cyclic of 2-power order, then for a minus module M and odd χ, M_χ ≅ M_{χ₀}, with χ₀ = χ|_{Δ₀}.
hypotheses: When p | |Δ| the χ-part is only right exact; this is why Greither's bounds carry controlled error terms, unlike Rubin's §III.2, which assumes p ∤ |Δ|.
proofSteps: Define M_χ by base change along ℤ_p[Δ] → ℤ_p(χ).
(a)–(d): standard. (e): χ(j) = −1 kills 1 + j. (f): the norm A_p(F) → A_p(F^+) is onto, so im M^+ = (1 + j)M.
(g): χ odd on a cyclic 2-group forces χ injective on Δ₂ with χ(j) = −1, so ℤ_2(χ) = ℤ_2[Δ₂]/(j + 1), and M_χ = M/(1 + j)M = M for a minus module.
acceptance: Greither's introductory example: an imaginary abelian field whose 2-class group (ℤ/2)^3 equals its minus part, on which the usual Stickelberger theorem says nothing about the Galois structure.

nodes.title: Semilocal units modulo circular units (Greither, Theorem 2.13 and Corollary 2.14)
nodes.statement: Let p any prime (p = 2 included), F/ℚ abelian and unramified at p, K_n = F(ζ_{2p^{n+1}}) (so K_0 = F(√−1) when p = 2), K_∞ = ∪K_n, Δ′ = Gal(K_0/ℚ), Γ = Gal(K_∞/K_0) ≅ ℤ_p, and Λ_χ = ℤ_p(χ)[[T]], and ρ an even nontrivial character of Δ′, with χ = ωρ^{−1}. Then Q_p ⊗ (U_∞/C_∞)_ρ and Q_p(χ)[[T]]/(G_p(T, ρ))*(1) have the same characteristic ideal over Q_pΛ_ρ, and they are isomorphic if χ(p) ≠ 1. Here U_∞ and C_∞ are the pro-p parts of the limits of semilocal units and of Sinnott's circular units, G_p(T, ρ) is Washington's f(T, ρ) with L_p(s, ρ) = G_p(u^s − 1, ρ), and * means Δ′ × Γ acts through the inverse. This is the form of Iwasawa's and Gillard's theorem for all p that Greither proves in §2.
hypotheses: The proof uses Coleman's theory adapted to unramified coefficients and p = 2 (L4/greither-coleman-sequence-all-p, L4/greither-semilocal-coleman-map). Coleman's own theorems are requested from ColemanPowerSeries L1 and L3.
Characteristic ideals are compared after ⊗Q_p, so only up to powers of p. The μ = 0 input of §3 removes these.
proofSteps: Theorem 2.13 (L4/greither-stickelberger-image) gives αψ(V_ρ(C_∞)) = G_p(T′, ρ)·z_{χ^{−1}}, and z_{χ^{−1}} is a free generator (Corollary 2.12). So V_ρ(𝒱(1))/αψ(V_ρ(C_∞)) ≅ ℚ_p(χ^{−1})[[T]]/(G_p(T′, ρ))(1), and T ↦ T′ turns it into (ℚ_p(χ)[[T]]/(G_p(T, ρ)))*(1).

Proposition 2.10 gives 0 → V_ρ(ℤ_p(1)^g) → V_ρ(U_∞/C_∞) → V_ρ(𝒱(1))/αψ(V_ρ(C_∞)) → V_ρ(ℤ_p(1)^g) → 0, using ℤ_p(1)^g ∩ C_∞ = ℤ_p(1) and V_ρ(ℤ_p(1)) = 0 since ρ ≠ ω. Since ℤ_p(1)^g ≅ ℤ_p[Δ/D] ⊗ ℤ_p(1), with D the decomposition group of p, the outer terms vanish when χ(p) ≠ 1.
Multiplicativity of characteristic ideals gives the corollary.
acceptance: χ(p) = 1 (p splits in the χ-field): isomorphism is lost, but equality of characteristic ideals remains.

nodes.title: The real main conjecture for all p (Greither, Theorem 3.1)
nodes.statement: Let p any prime (p = 2 included), F/ℚ abelian and unramified at p, K_n = F(ζ_{2p^{n+1}}) (so K_0 = F(√−1) when p = 2), K_∞ = ∪K_n, Δ′ = Gal(K_0/ℚ), Γ = Gal(K_∞/K_0) ≅ ℤ_p, and Λ_χ = ℤ_p(χ)[[T]]. For every even character ρ ≠ 1 of K_0, the characteristic ideal of the Λ_ρ-module X_ρ (X = lim A_p(K_n)) divides the characteristic ideal of (E_∞/C_∞)_ρ, where E_∞ is the limit of the pro-p parts of the closures of the global units. For ρ = 1 both are (1). Equality holds, as a by-product of the proof of Theorem 3.2. X and E_∞/C_∞ may be replaced by their plus parts.
hypotheses: The proof is Kolyvagin–Rubin's Euler system of circular units (Rubin, Invent. Math. 103 (1991)). Every circular number starts an Euler system (Greither §3, via Lemma 2.3).
For p = 2, Rubin's Chebotarev step is replaced by Greither's Theorem 3.7 (L4/greither-chebotarev-at-two), which loses a factor 2^{c+2}, or 4 at the layers K_n^+.
Factors of p and (γ − 1) accumulate through Lemmas 3.9–3.13; they are removed at the end using μ = 0 (Ferrero–Washington) and Leopoldt for real abelian fields.
proofSteps: Reduce to plus parts and to even χ ≠ 1: for χ = 1, X_χ is quasi-isomorphic to lim A(ℚ_ν) = 0.

Fix n, K = K_n^+, h a power of p with h ≥ |Λ_{n,χ}/(H_χ)|, |Λ_{n,χ}/(ord Δ)|, |Λ_{n,χ}/(p)|, and M = |A_χ|·h^{3k+ck+1} with c = max(c_1, c_2). By Lemma 3.10 choose c_i ∈ A_χ with τ_n(c_i) = p^{c_2} in the i-th place; then p^{c_2}·Ann(c_i in A_χ/(c_1, …, c_{i−1})) ⊆ g_iΛ_{n,χ}. By Lemma 3.9 choose a circular unit ξ with ϑ_n(ξ) = (γ − 1)²p^{c_1}H_χ, and an Euler system starting with ξ.

Construct primes λ_1, …, λ_{k+1} of K inductively (Corollary 3.8, Lemmas 3.12–3.13) with [λ_i]_χ = p²c_i, ℓ_i ∈ 𝒮_{M,K}, v_{λ_1}(κ_{ℓ_1}) = unit·|Δ|·(γ − 1)²p^{2+c_1}H_χ, and for 2 ≤ i ≤ k + 1: g_{i−1}·v_{λ_i}(κ_{r_i}) = unit·|Δ|·p^{2+c_2}(γ − 1)^{2^{i−1}}·v_{λ_{i−1}}(κ_{r_{i−1}}). At step i, apply Lemma 3.12 with η = (γ − 1)^{2^{i−1}} and E = p^{c_2}; its hypothesis (iii) is the bound on N = (γ − 1)^{2^{i−1}}(𝒥_{ℓ_{i−1}}/(M, (κ_{r_{i−1}})_{[ℓ_{i−1}]})), where Greither prints the exponent as 2^t (source issue E17).

Multiplying out gives g_1⋯g_k·v_{λ_{k+1}}(κ_{r_{k+1}}) = |Δ|^{k+1}p^{k(2+c_2)+(2+c_1)}(γ − 1)^{2^{k+1}}·H_χ = η·H_χ in Λ_{n,χ}/(M). So g divides ηH_χ in Λ_{n,χ}/(p^n) for every n, and hence in Λ_χ (as in Rubin).
By Lemma 3.11 and μ = 0 (Ferrero–Washington), η acts on X_χ with finite kernel and cokernel, so η and g are coprime in ℚ_pΛ_χ: p^N = aη + bg. Hence g | p^N·H_χ, and since μ = 0, p ∤ g, so g | H_χ.
acceptance: For odd p and p ∤ [F : ℚ] this is Rubin's III.2.7 (L2/cyclotomic-iwasawa-divisibility).

nodes.title: Kummer duality between the odd and even sides (Greither, Lemma 3.3 and Proposition 3.4)
nodes.statement: Let p any prime (p = 2 included), F/ℚ abelian and unramified at p, K_n = F(ζ_{2p^{n+1}}) (so K_0 = F(√−1) when p = 2), K_∞ = ∪K_n, Δ′ = Gal(K_0/ℚ), Γ = Gal(K_∞/K_0) ≅ ℤ_p, and Λ_χ = ℤ_p(χ)[[T]]. X = lim A_p(K_n) is quasi-isomorphic over Λ to Hom_{ℤ_p}(A_∞, ℚ_p/ℤ_p), where A_∞ = lim→ A_p(K_n) and Λ acts through σ ↦ σ, not its inverse (Lemma 3.3, after Iwasawa and Solomon). For each even ρ, with χ = ωρ^{−1}: V_ρ(Y^+) ≅ V_χ(X)*(1), where Y is the Galois group of the maximal abelian p-ramified p-extension of K_∞ and V = Q_p ⊗ (·) (Proposition 3.4).
hypotheses: Greenberg analyses the Kummer pairing at p = 2 without ⊗Q_p; Greither tensors with Q_p for simplicity, so the duality holds up to finite and p-power errors.
proofSteps: Lemma 3.3 from Iwasawa's quasi-isomorphism over Λ, as in Solomon.
Proposition 3.4 from the Kummer pairing between Y^+ and A_∞, as in Greenberg.
acceptance: The twist (1) and the inversion * are what exchange even ρ with odd χ = ωρ^{−1}.

nodes.title: The main conjecture for all p, with the one-half normalisation (Greither, Theorem 3.2)
nodes.statement: Let p any prime (p = 2 included), F/ℚ abelian and unramified at p, K_n = F(ζ_{2p^{n+1}}) (so K_0 = F(√−1) when p = 2), K_∞ = ∪K_n, Δ′ = Gal(K_0/ℚ), Γ = Gal(K_∞/K_0) ≅ ℤ_p, and Λ_χ = ℤ_p(χ)[[T]], and X = lim A_p(K_n), X^+ = lim A_p(K_n^+). For every odd character χ ≠ ω of K_0 (with χ̌ = ωχ^{−1}), (X/im X^+)_χ ≅ X_χ canonically, and char(X_χ) = ((1/2)·G_p(T, χ̌)) as ideals of Λ_χ = ℤ_p(χ)[[T]] if χ̌ is nontrivial; if χ̌ is trivial, char(X_χ) = ((1/2)·G_p(T, χ̌)·(T − q₀)) = (1). For odd p, 1/2 is a unit, and this is the Mazur–Wiles theorem in odd-character form; for p = 2 the factor 1/2 is essential.
hypotheses: (1/2)G_p(T, ψ) ∈ ℤ_p(ψ)[[T]] for nontrivial ψ, and (1/2)G_p(T, ψ)(T − q₀) is a unit for trivial ψ (Washington pp. 122–125). This is the normalisation Federer gives.
proofSteps: Two exact sequences: 0 → U_∞/E_∞ → Y → X → 0 (class field theory) and 0 → E_∞/C_∞ → U_∞/C_∞ → U_∞/E_∞ → 0.
By Theorem 3.1, h_ρ·char(X_ρ) = char((E_∞/C_∞)_ρ). With Corollary 2.14, h_ρ·char(Y_ρ) = char(U_∞/C_∞)_ρ = char(Λ/(½G_p(T, ρ))*(1)).
Proposition 3.4 converts char(Y_ρ^+) into char(X_χ*(1)), so char(X_χ) divides (½G_p(T, χ̌)) for every odd χ ≠ ω.
X_ω is finite (for odd p by Mazur–Wiles p. 183; for p = 2, F = ℚ or ℚ(i) gives X = 0).
The analytic class number formula for minus class groups turns the divisibilities into equalities (Greenberg).
acceptance: χ = ω is excluded: that component is finite, and there char is (1).
For p = 2 the characteristic ideal is that of ½G₂, not of G₂.

nodes.title: Classes of the primes above p, and injectivity of E⁺ → E (Greither, Lemma 4.2 and Corollary 4.3)
nodes.statement: Let p be a prime and F an imaginary abelian field such that p splits completely in F, every prime of F above p is totally ramified in the cyclotomic ℤ_p-extension F_∞/F, and μ_{p^∞}(F_∞) is finite; let Δ = Gal(F/ℚ), j complex conjugation and Γ = Gal(F_∞/F). Let B_n be the subgroup of the divisor group of F_n generated by the primes above p, D_n its image in A_n = A_p(F_n), D_∞ = lim D_n, and D_∞^+ the same for F_n^+. Then D_∞/im D_∞^+ ≅ ℤ_p[Δ]/(1 + j)ℤ_p[Δ] as ℤ_p[Δ][[Γ]]-modules, with Γ acting trivially on the right (Lemma 4.2). For p = 2, with X = lim A_n, E = X/D_∞ ≅ lim A_n/D_n (a quotient of class groups, not a unit group) and E^+ the same for F^+, the canonical map E^+ → E is injective (Corollary 4.3).
hypotheses: Lemma 4.2 uses only the three hypotheses above (Greither's parenthesis before the lemma), so it holds for every p; Corollary 4.3 is stated for p = 2.
proofSteps: Fix a norm-coherent sequence 𝔭_n of primes above p in F_n, and let h be the p-class number of F. The projective system B_n/(hB_0 + B_n^+) is isomorphic to (ℤ/hp^nℤ)[Δ]/(1 + j) via 1 ↦ 𝔭_n; hB_0 maps to 0 in D_n.
It is enough that the kernels of α_n: B_n/(hB_0 + B_n^+) → D_n/im D_n^+ have bounded order, which follows from |D_n|/|D_n^+| ≥ const·p^{n|Δ|/2}.

Apply the ambiguous-class formula for a cyclic extension K/F′ (Lang, Cyclotomic Fields II, Chapter 13 §4, formulas (2)–(3)) to (F_n, F) and (F_n^+, F^+). The products of ramification indices are e(F_n/F) = p^{n|Δ|} and e(F_n^+/F^+) = p^{n|Δ|/2}. The two unit norm indices differ by a bounded factor because F has only finitely many p-power roots of unity.
The kernels have bounded order and the limit ℤ_p[Δ]/(1 + j) is ℤ_p-torsion-free, so lim α_n is an isomorphism.

Corollary 4.3: from the rows 0 → D_∞^± → X^± → E^± → 0 it suffices that D_∞ ∩ im X^+ = im D_∞^+. On Q = (D_∞ ∩ im X^+)/im D_∞^+, j acts as +1 (Q lies in the image of X^+) and as −1 (Q lies in D_∞/im D_∞^+ ≅ ℤ_2[Δ]/(1 + j)). That module has no 2-torsion, so Q = 0.
acceptance: Γ acts trivially on D_∞/im D_∞^+, so for odd χ its χ-part has characteristic ideal (T) over Λ_χ (used in the trivial-zero reduction).

nodes.title: The trivial-zero reduction when χ(2) = 1 (Greither, Lemma 4.4, Proposition 4.5 and (***))
nodes.statement: Let p = 2, F an imaginary abelian field unramified at 2 with Δ = Gal(F/ℚ) = Δ_2 × Δ_0, Δ_2 cyclic and |Δ_0| odd, j complex conjugation, F_n the layers of the cyclotomic ℤ_2-extension, A_n = A_2(F_n), and χ an odd character of Δ, injective on Δ, with χ(2) = 1 (so 2 splits completely in F) and ξ = χ|Δ_0 nontrivial; χ̌ = ωχ^{−1} and Λ_χ = ℤ_2(χ)[[T]]. Let E_n = A_n/D_n and E_n^+ = A_n^+/D_n^+. For a module M and x ∈ ℤ_2[[Γ]] write M_x = M/xM, and M^{(x)} for the kernel of x. Let γ generate Γ and T = γ − 1. Define Z and Z^+ as the kernels in the rows 0 → Z^+ → (E^+)_{1−γ} → E_0^+ → 0 and 0 → Z → E_{1−γ} → E_0 → 0, with vertical maps α, β and ε. Then: (Lemma 4.4) if Z/im Z^+ is finite, |ker β| ≤ |(E/E^+)^{(1−γ)}| < ∞; (Proposition 4.5) |½G′_2(0, χ̌)|_2^{d(χ)} ≤ (|E_{0ξ}|/|E^+_{0ξ}|)·|(Z/Z^+)_ξ|, where ′ = d/dT; and hence (***) |A(F)_χ| = |(A_0)_ξ|/|(A_0^+)_ξ| ≥ |½G′_2(0, χ̌)|_2^{d(χ)}·|(Z/im Z^+)_ξ|^{−1}·|(D_0)_ξ|/|(D_0^+)_ξ|.
hypotheses: Greither writes |x|_p = p^{v(x)} with v(p) = 1, so |x|_p^{d(χ)} is the order of ℤ_p(χ)/xℤ_p(χ); an inequality between such orders is a divisibility of 2-powers.
|Δ_0| is odd, so (·)_ξ is exact on ℤ_2[Δ_0]-modules, and (**) and Lemma 4.4 hold after taking ξ-parts.
proofSteps: (**) The snake lemma, with |E_0|·|E_0^+|^{−1} = |coker ε|·|ker ε|^{−1}, gives |(E/E^+)_{1−γ}| = |coker β| ≤ |ker β|·|E_0|·|E_0^+|^{−1}·|Z/im Z^+|; the inequality drops |ker α|^{−1}.

Lemma 4.4. The norm F_n → F_n^+ gives β′ with β′β = 2, so ker β is killed by 2. It is finite because E^+, a quotient of X^+, is finitely generated over ℤ_2. Since E_0 is finite, the hypothesis makes (E/E^+)_{1−γ} finite, so T has finite kernel and cokernel on E/E^+. The sequence Tor^Λ(Λ/(T), E/E^+) → (E^+)_{1−γ} → E_{1−γ} → (E/E^+)_{1−γ} → 0 bounds ker β by the Tor term, which is (E/E^+)^{(1−γ)}.

Proposition 4.5. Corollary 4.3 and the snake lemma give 0 → (D_∞/D_∞^+)_ξ → (X/im X^+)_ξ → (E/E^+)_ξ → 0, and ξ may be replaced by χ in all three terms. char((D_∞/D_∞^+)_χ) = (T) by Lemma 4.2, and char((X/im X^+)_χ) = (½G_2(T, χ̌)) by Theorem 3.2. So ½G_2(T, χ̌) is divisible by T, the trivial zero forced by χ(2) = 1, and char((E/E^+)_χ) = (½G_2(T, χ̌)·T^{−1}).

The coinvariant lemma (Coates, Lemma 9) gives |coker β_ξ| = |(E/E^+)_{ξ,1−γ}| = |(E/E^+)^{(1−γ)}_ξ|·|½G′_2(0, χ̌)|_2^{d(χ)}. Combine this with (**) and the ξ-version of Lemma 4.4. If (Z/Z^+)_ξ is infinite, the proposition is trivial.
(***) |E_0|/|E_0^+| = |A_0|·|A_0^+|^{−1}·|D_0|^{−1}·|D_0^+|, also in ξ-parts. Since ξ is nontrivial, (A_0^+)_ξ → A_{0ξ} and (D_0^+)_ξ → D_{0ξ} are injective, and |(A_0)_ξ|/|(A_0^+)_ξ| = |A(F)_χ|.
acceptance: The inequality bounds |A(F)_χ| from below. The trivial-zero formula identifies the right side of (***) with |½B_{1,χ^{−1}}|_2^{d(χ)}.

nodes.title: Z/Z⁺ as a quotient of 2-adic semilocal units (Greither, Proposition 4.7)
nodes.statement: Let p = 2, F an imaginary abelian field unramified at 2 with Δ = Gal(F/ℚ) = Δ_2 × Δ_0, Δ_2 cyclic and |Δ_0| odd, j complex conjugation, F_n the layers of the cyclotomic ℤ_2-extension, A_n = A_2(F_n), and χ an odd character of Δ, injective on Δ, with χ(2) = 1 (so 2 splits completely in F) and ξ = χ|Δ_0 nontrivial; χ̌ = ωχ^{−1} and Λ_χ = ℤ_2(χ)[[T]]. With Z, Z^+ as in the trivial-zero reduction, fix a prime 𝔭 of F above 2. The primes above 2 are 𝔭_δ = 𝔭^δ (δ ∈ Δ), and (ℚ_2 ⊗ F)^× = (ℚ_2^×)^Δ. Let V = {±1} × 2^ℤ ⊂ ℚ_2^×, N(F) = (ℚ_2 ⊗ F)^×/closure(O_F[1/2]^×)·V^Δ, and N(F^+) the same with Δ^+ = Δ/{1, j}. N(F) is a quotient of (ℤ_2^×)^Δ. Then (a) there is a natural isomorphism Z_ξ ≅ N(F)_ξ, and likewise Z^+_ξ ≅ N(F^+)_ξ; (b) (Z/im Z^+)_χ ≅ (N(F)/N(F^+))_χ ≅ N(F)_χ.
proofSteps: Let L be the maximal unramified abelian 2-extension of F_∞ in which every prime above 2 splits completely, so Gal(L/F_∞) ≅ E = X/D_∞ by class field theory. Let L_0 be the same over F, so Gal(L_0/F) ≅ E_0. Put M = L ∩ F^ab, G = Gal(L/F) and G/G′ = Gal(M/F).

Claim: Gal(M/L_0) ≅ N(F). M is the maximal abelian 2-ramified 2-extension of F that is unramified over F_∞ and in which every prime above 2 has inertial degree one. It corresponds to a closed subgroup H of C_2(F) = J_F/F^×·∏_{q∤2}U_q. Decomposition equals inertia at each 𝔭_δ, which forces (2·u_δ^{−1})^{(δ)} ∈ H with u_δ ∈ {±1}, and M/F_∞ unramified gives (−1)^{(δ)} ∈ H. So H is the image of V^Δ.
Hence Gal(M/F) = C_2(F)/im V^Δ, and 0 → N(F) → G/G′ → E_0 → 0 is exact.

With 0 → E_{1−γ} → G/G′ → Γ → 0 (Washington, Lemma 13.14) and Δ acting trivially on Γ, Γ_ξ = 0. So E_{ξ,1−γ} ≅ (G/G′)_ξ, and N(F)_ξ ≅ ker(E_{ξ,1−γ} → E_{0ξ}) = Z_ξ. This is (a); the argument for F^+ is the same.
(b) Naturality of (a) for F and F^+ gives (Z/im Z^+)_ξ ≅ (N(F)/N(F^+))_ξ. Since j acts as −1 on the right side, ξ may be replaced by χ on both sides.
acceptance: Γ carries the trivial Δ-action, so Γ_ξ = 0 for ξ ≠ 1; this is where the nontriviality of ξ enters.

nodes.title: The Gauss-sum 2-unit with its valuation and logarithm vectors (Greither, (G1), (G2) and Lemma 4.8)
nodes.statement: Let p = 2, F an imaginary abelian field unramified at 2 with Δ = Gal(F/ℚ) = Δ_2 × Δ_0, Δ_2 cyclic and |Δ_0| odd, j complex conjugation, F_n the layers of the cyclotomic ℤ_2-extension, A_n = A_2(F_n), and χ an odd character of Δ, injective on Δ, with χ(2) = 1 (so 2 splits completely in F) and ξ = χ|Δ_0 nontrivial; χ̌ = ωχ^{−1} and Λ_χ = ℤ_2(χ)[[T]]. Let W = O_F[1/2]^×/O_{F^+}[1/2]^×. Let M be the free ℤ_2-module on the 𝔭_δ modulo the span of the 𝔭_δ + 𝔭_{δj}, so M ≅ ℤ_2[Δ]/(1 + j). Define μ: W → M, u ↦ Σ_δ v_{𝔭_δ}(u)·𝔭_δ, and λ: W → 4M, u ↦ Σ_δ log_2(u^{δ^{−1}})·𝔭_δ, where log_2: F → F_𝔭 = ℚ_2 and log_2(ℤ_2^×) = 4ℤ_2. Let m be the conductor of F (odd), 𝔓 a prime of ℚ(μ_m) above 𝔭, f = ord(2 mod m), η the m-th power residue symbol at 𝔓, ψ the nontrivial additive character of 𝔽_2, and g = −Σ_a η^{−1}(a)ψ(Tr a) the Gauss sum. Let D be the decomposition field of 2 in ℚ(μ_m), so F ⊆ D and g ∈ D, and put g_F = N_{D/F}(g) ∈ F, a 2-unit. With ⟨g_F⟩ its ℤ_2Δ-span in W: (G1) μ_χ(g_F) = B_{1,χ^{−1}}·(𝔭)_χ (Stickelberger); (G2) λ_χ(g_F) = 4·G′_2(0, χ̌)·unit·(𝔭)_χ, by Gross–Koblitz, Ferrero–Greenberg and Lemma 4.8 (Σ_{(b,m)=1} χ^{−1}(b)ζ_2(b, s) = L_2(s, χ̌) as meromorphic functions on ℤ_2), with L_2(s, χ̌) = G_2(u^s − 1, χ̌) and log_2(u) associated to 4. Both μ_χ(g_F) and λ_χ(g_F) are nonzero.
hypotheses: Greither takes g itself and asserts g ∈ F. In general g lies only in D, and D can be larger than F (source issue E5). Its norm g_F is what his sums over all b with (b, m) = 1 compute, and it equals g when F = D.
Greither's (G1) and μ_χ carry an extra factor m and drop b from the exponent (source issue E6). m is odd, so this does not change any 2-adic order.
proofSteps: g is fixed by σ_2, since Tr(a²) = Tr(a) (Frobenius invariance), so g ∈ D, where 2 splits completely. F ⊆ D because 2 splits completely in F.

(G1) By Stickelberger's theorem at p = 2, (g) = ∏_{b ∈ (ℤ/m)^×/⟨2⟩} (σ_b^{−1}𝔓)^{Σ_{t=1}^{f}⟨2^t b/m⟩}. Taking N_{D/F} collects all b with σ_b|_F = δ: μ(g_F) = Σ_δ Σ_{b mod m, σ_b ↦ δ} ⟨b/m⟩·𝔭_{δ^{−1}}, and μ_χ(g_F) = (Σ_b ⟨b/m⟩χ^{−1}(b))·(𝔭)_χ = B_{1,χ^{−1}}·(𝔭)_χ, since χ has conductor m.

(G2) λ_χ(g_F) = (Σ_δ log_2(g_F^δ)·χ^{−1}(δ))·(𝔭)_χ. Gross–Koblitz writes each conjugate of g as a product of Morita Γ_2-values, so this is Σ_{(b,m)=1} χ^{−1}(b)·log_2 Γ_2(⟨b/m⟩)·(𝔭)_χ. Ferrero–Greenberg (Gross [10], p. 993) turns it into Σ_{(b,m)=1} χ^{−1}(b)·ζ′_2(b, 0)·(𝔭)_χ.

Lemma 4.8 identifies the last sum with L′_2(0, χ̌)·(𝔭)_χ. It suffices to check s = 1 − n for odd n ∈ ℕ, using the definitions (Washington, Chapter 5; Gross [10], p. 989). Then L′_2(0, χ̌) = log_2(u)·G′_2(0, χ̌), and log_2(u) is associated to 4.
μ_χ(g_F) ≠ 0 because B_{1,χ^{−1}} ≠ 0 for odd χ. λ_χ(g_F) ≠ 0 by Gross [10], 1.15, a consequence of his Conjecture 2.12, which he proves for abelian fields.
acceptance: The index computations in the trivial-zero formula use only the ℤ_2(χ)-lines spanned by μ_χ(g_F) and λ_χ(g_F), so units (including m) do not matter.

nodes.title: The trivial-zero formula (Greither, Lemmas 4.9–4.10 and Theorem 4.6)
nodes.statement: Let p = 2, F an imaginary abelian field unramified at 2 with Δ = Gal(F/ℚ) = Δ_2 × Δ_0, Δ_2 cyclic and |Δ_0| odd, j complex conjugation, F_n the layers of the cyclotomic ℤ_2-extension, A_n = A_2(F_n), and χ an odd character of Δ, injective on Δ, with χ(2) = 1 (so 2 splits completely in F) and ξ = χ|Δ_0 nontrivial; χ̌ = ωχ^{−1} and Λ_χ = ℤ_2(χ)[[T]]. With Z, Z^+, D_0 as in the trivial-zero reduction and μ, λ as in the Gauss-sum construction: (Lemma 4.9) |coker(λ_χ: W′_χ → 4ℤ_2(χ))| = |(Z/im Z^+)_χ|, where W′_χ is the 2-adic completion of W_χ modulo 2-torsion, of rank one over ℤ_2(χ); (Lemma 4.10) |coker μ_χ| = |(D_0/im D_0^+)_χ|; and (Theorem 4.6) |½G′_2(0, χ̌)|_2^{d(χ)}·|(Z/im Z^+)_ξ|^{−1}·|(D_0)_ξ|/|(D_0^+)_ξ| = |½B_{1,χ^{−1}}|_2^{d(χ)}.
proofSteps: ℚ_2 ⊗ W ≅ ℚ_2Δ/(1 + j), so ℚ_2 ⊗ W_χ ≅ ℚ_2(χ), and λ_χ, μ_χ induce monomorphisms W′_χ → M_χ ≅ ℤ_2(χ).

Lemma 4.9. Compare W′_χ → 4ℤ_2(χ) with V^Δ → ((ℚ_2F)^×/(ℚ_2F^+)^×)_χ → 4ℤ_2(χ), where λ′ is λ on (ℚ_2^×)^Δ. Since ker(log_2: ℚ_2^× → 4ℤ_2) = V, the lower sequence is exact. So coker λ_χ ≅ (N(F)/N(F^+))_χ, which is (Z/im Z^+)_χ by Proposition 4.7(b).
Lemma 4.10. The definition of μ gives coker μ ≅ D_0/im D_0^+ naturally.

Theorem 4.6. |(Z/im Z^+)_χ|^{−1}·|(D_0/im D_0^+)_χ| = |coker λ_χ|^{−1}·|coker μ_χ|. Computing both indices through the lines spanned by λ_χ(⟨g_F⟩) and μ_χ(⟨g_F⟩), the factors |W′_χ/⟨g_F⟩| cancel, and (G1), (G2) give |G′_2(0, χ̌)|_2^{−d(χ)}·|B_{1,χ^{−1}}|_2^{d(χ)}. Multiplying by |½|_2^{d(χ)} on both sides and using injectivity of (D_0^+)_ξ → D_{0ξ} gives 4.6.
acceptance: The ½ cancels between the two sides of 4.6; the content is |(Z/im Z^+)_χ|^{−1}·|(D_0/im D_0^+)_χ| = |G′_2(0, χ̌)|_2^{−d(χ)}·|B_{1,χ^{−1}}|_2^{d(χ)}.

nodes.title: |A₂(F)_χ| is divisible by |½B_{1,χ⁻¹}|^{d(χ)} (Greither, Theorem 4.1 = Theorem B)
nodes.statement: Let p = 2 and F an imaginary abelian field unramified at 2 with Δ = Gal(F/ℚ) = Δ_2 × Δ_0 and Δ_2 cyclic. For every odd character χ of Δ, |A_2(F)_χ| ≥ |½B_{1,χ^{−1}}|_2^{d(χ)}, that is, the 2-power |A_2(F)_χ| is divisible by |½B_{1,χ^{−1}}|_2^{d(χ)} = 2^{d(χ)·v_2(½B_{1,χ^{−1}})}. Here A_2(F)_χ ≅ (A_2(F)/im A_2(F^+))_χ ≅ A_2(F)^−_χ, since χ is odd and the norm A_2(F) → A_2(F^+) is onto.
hypotheses: Greither states Theorem 4.1 for every p and χ faithful on Δ_p. For odd p he cites Mazur–Wiles (|Δ| prime to p) and Solomon (general case), neither read here, and says the argument below works for all p. The node is the case p = 2 (Theorem B), where every odd χ is faithful on the cyclic Δ_2.
proofSteps: χ(j) = −1 makes χ injective on Δ_2, so ker χ ⊂ Δ_0. Replace F by the fixed field of ker χ, so that χ is injective on Δ.

Case χ(2) ≠ 1. Let D be the decomposition group of 2 in Δ, Δ̄ = Δ/D, γ a topological generator of Γ and γ_n = γ^{p^n}. As in Washington p. 278 there is an exact sequence 0 → ((1 − γ_n)/(1 − γ))·Y_0/(1 − γ_n)X → X/(1 − γ_n)X → A(K_n) → 0, whose first term is a quotient of Z = Y_0/(1 − γ)X.

With L and G = Gal(L/F) as on Washington p. 277, 𝔓 a prime of L above a divisor 𝔭 of p and σ a generator of its inertia group, Z is the ℤ_p-span of the z_τ = [σ^τσ^{−1}] (τ ∈ Gal(L/ℚ)). z_τ = 0 for τ ∈ G, so Z is a quotient of the augmentation ideal of ℤ_pΔ; it is cyclic because Δ_p is cyclic, and D acts trivially, so Z is a quotient of ℤ_pΔ̄. Taking χ-parts gives (ℤ_pΔ̄)_χ → X_χ/(1 − γ_n)X_χ → A(K_n)_χ → 0. The Frobenius at 2 acts on the left term trivially and by χ(2), so that term is cyclic over ℤ_2(χ), killed by 1 − χ(2), of order at most |1 − χ(2)|_2^{d(χ)}.

Case χ(2) = 1. Then 2 splits completely in F. (***) of the trivial-zero reduction and Theorem 4.6 give |A(F)_χ| ≥ |½G′_2(0, χ̌)|_2^{d(χ)}·|(Z/im Z^+)_ξ|^{−1}·|(D_0)_ξ|/|(D_0^+)_ξ| = |½B_{1,χ^{−1}}|_2^{d(χ)}.
acceptance: When χ is not of 2-power order, equality holds; this is Theorem A.
For χ of 2-power order, |A(F)_χ| = 2·|½B_{1,χ^{−1}}|_2^{d(χ)} (p. 482), strictly larger than the bound.

nodes.title: The Iwasawa–Leopoldt conjecture at p = 2 (Greither, Theorem A)
nodes.statement: Let F/ℚ be an imaginary abelian field unramified at 2 with Galois group Δ = Δ_2 × Δ_0, Δ_2 cyclic and |Δ_0| odd. For every odd 2-adic character χ of Δ that is not of 2-power order (that is, χ|Δ_0 ≠ ε), |A_2(F)^−_χ| = |½B_{1,χ^{−1}}|_2^{d(χ)}, where A_2(F)^− = {x ∈ A_2(F): x^j = −x}, d(χ) = [ℤ_2(χ):ℤ_2] and |a|_2 = 2^e for a = 2^e·u ∈ ℤ_2(χ) with u a unit. For the single odd character χ_2 of 2-power order (up to ℚ_2-conjugacy), with L the fixed field of Δ_0, |A_2(F)_{χ_2}| = |A_2(L)^−| = 2·|½B_{1,χ_2^{−1}}|_2^{d(χ_2)}·k_L, where k_L = |ker(A_2(L^+) → A_2(L))| = 1. Consequently (1 − e_ε)A_2(F)^− is annihilated by ½ times the images in (1 − e_ε)ℤ_2[Δ]/(1 + j) of the Stickelberger elements of F, which sharpens Stickelberger's theorem at 2.
hypotheses: The characters χ are taken up to ℚ_2-conjugacy, and each class contributes one factor with exponent d(χ).
proofSteps: For each odd χ with χ|Δ_0 ≠ ε, |A_2(F)^−_χ| = |(A_2(F)/im A_2(F^+))_χ|. For a cyclic 2-group Δ_2 the minus quotient ℤ_2(χ_0)[Δ_2]/(1 + j) is the domain ℤ_2(χ); see the χ-parts node, property (g).

The analytic class number formula for F and for L (with Q_L = 1 and w_L = 2) and k_F = k_L give |(1 − e_ε)A_2(F)^−| = ∏ |½B_{1,χ^{−1}}|_2^{d(χ)} over the odd χ with χ|Δ_0 ≠ ε, modulo ℚ_2-conjugacy. The same product of the |A_2(F)^−_χ| equals |(1 − e_ε)A_2(F)^−|, because ξ-parts are exact.
Theorem B bounds each factor below; the products agree, so every factor is an equality.

k_L = 1. Every nontrivial subgroup of the cyclic 2-group Gal(L/ℚ) contains j, and some odd prime ℓ ramifies in L, so L/L^+ is ramified above ℓ. L is unramified at 2, so i ∉ L, and μ(L)/μ(L)² is generated by −1. Let 𝔞 be a class of L^+ with 𝔞O_L = (α). Then α/ᾱ is a unit of absolute value 1 everywhere, so a root of unity. If α/ᾱ = ζ² = ζ/ζ̄, then α/ζ ∈ L^+ generates 𝔞, which is trivial. Otherwise α can be rescaled so that ᾱ = −α. Then δ = α² ∈ L^+, L = L^+(√δ) and δO_{L^+} = 𝔞², so v_𝔮(δ) is even at every 𝔮 above ℓ. This contradicts the ramification of L/L^+ above ℓ.
The annihilation statement: for (1 − e_ε)A_2(F)^− the χ-parts are cyclic of order |½B_{1,χ^{−1}}|_2^{d(χ)}, the χ-component of ½ times a Stickelberger element.
acceptance: Examples show some condition on Δ_2 is necessary (Greither, Remark a)).

nodes.title: Ray class groups of real abelian fields and ½L_p(1, χ) (Greither, Theorem 4.11)
nodes.statement: Let F be a real abelian field and p a prime unramified in F, with Δ = Gal(F/ℚ) = Δ_p × Δ_0 and Δ_p the p-part. Let A′(F) = lim_ν C_{(p^ν)}(F), where C_{(p^ν)}(F) is the p-part of the ray class group modulo p^ν. Let e = e_ε = |Δ_0|^{−1}Σ_{δ∈Δ_0}δ. Then (1 − e)A′(F) is finite, and for every character χ_0 ≠ 1 of Δ_0, |A′(F)_{χ_0}| = ∏_{χ|Δ_0 = χ_0} |½L_p(1, χ)|_p^{d(χ)}, the product over the characters χ of Δ restricting to χ_0, taken up to conjugacy over ℚ_p(χ_0). Equivalently, as in the proof, the product runs over all such χ with exponent d(χ_0).
hypotheses: Leopoldt's conjecture for F and p (true for abelian F) is used to identify A′(F) with Y/TY and to make (1 − e)A′(F) finite.
proofSteps: Y = lim A′(F_n) is the Galois group of the maximal abelian p-ramified p-extension of F_∞, a Λ_Δ-module with A′(F) ≅ Y/TY. Define T̂ by 1 + T̂ = u·(1 + T)^{−1}. By Theorem 3.2 and Proposition 3.4, char_{Λ_χ}(Y_χ) = ½G_p(T̂, χ)Λ_χ for every χ, so char_{Λ_{χ_0}}(Y_{χ_0}) = (∏_χ ½G_p(T̂, χ)) over χ|Δ_0 = χ_0.
Let δ(χ_0) be the order of the T-coinvariants of the torsion of Y_{χ_0}. Iwasawa theory gives |A′_{χ_0}| = ∏_χ |½G_p(T̂, χ)|_{T=0}|_p^{d(χ_0)}·δ(χ_0) = ∏_χ |½L_p(1, χ)|_p^{d(χ_0)}·δ(χ_0).
It suffices that ∏_{χ_0 ≠ 1}|A′_{χ_0}| = ∏_{χ|Δ_0 ≠ 1}|½L_p(1, χ)|_p; then every δ(χ_0) = 1. The left side is |(1 − e)A′| = |A′(F)|/|A′(L)|, with L the fixed field of Δ_0.

0 → (1 − e)(U_F/Ē_F) → (1 − e)A′(F) → (1 − e)A(F) → 0, and |(1 − e)(U_F/Ē_F)| = p^{−[F:ℚ]+[L:ℚ]}·R_p(F)·R_p(L)^{−1}. The proof compares log_p: (1 − e)U_F → (1 − e)p(ℤ_p ⊗ O_F), whose kernel and cokernel have equal order (1 for odd p, 2^{g(F)−g(L)} for p = 2, g the number of primes above 2), and uses (1 − e)Ē_F ∩ ker log_p = 0.

The p-adic class number formula for F and for L (Washington, Theorem 5.24) gives the quotient (2p)^{…}·(d(F)/d(L))^{1/2}·∏(1 − p^{−1}χ(p))^{−1}·½L_p(1, χ). F and L are unramified at p and χ(p) ≠ 0, so its p-value is that of ∏_{χ|Δ_0 ≠ 1}½L_p(1, χ).
acceptance: Every δ(χ_0) = 1: the torsion of Y_{χ_0} has trivial T-coinvariants for χ_0 ≠ 1.
For p = 2 the kernel and cokernel of log_2 on (1 − e)U_F both have order 2^{g(F)−g(L)}; for odd p both are trivial.

nodes.title: Norm and inclusion maps on p-adic ray class groups (Greither, Lemma 4.13)
nodes.statement: Let F/K be a p-extension of cyclic number fields that are unramified above p, with C = Gal(F/K). There are Galois-equivariant homomorphisms α: A′(F) → A′(K), induced by N_{F/K}, and β: A′(K) → A′(F), induced by K ⊂ F, such that α is surjective, β is injective, and βα is multiplication by the norm element Σ_{σ∈C}σ.
proofSteps: Gal(F/ℚ) is cyclic and generated by inertia groups, so some prime ℓ ≠ p ramifies totally in F/ℚ. Hence F/K has no p-ramified subextension, and α is onto.
For a divisor 𝔪 of K, ker(C_𝔪(K) → C_𝔪(F)) embeds into H¹(C, E_𝔪(F)) with E_𝔪(F) = ker(O_F^× → (O_F/𝔪O_F)^×). Since lim is left exact, it suffices that lim_ν H¹(C, E_{(p^ν)}(F)) = 0.
Leopoldt's conjecture for p and F gives N ≥ 2 such that every x ∈ E_{(p^{N+1})}(F) is a p-th power of a unit y, and y ∈ E_{(p^N)}(F) because p is unramified in F.

Let p^c = |C| and ν ≥ N. Every 1-cocycle x = (x_σ) in Z¹(C, E_{(p^{ν+c})}(F)) has x_σ = y_σ^{p^c} with y_σ ∈ E_{(p^ν)}(F). E_{(p^ν)}(F) contains no nontrivial p-power root of unity: for odd p because F is unramified at p, and for p = 2 because −1 ≢ 1 mod 4 and ν ≥ 2. So (y_σ) is again a cocycle, and the image of x in H¹(C, E_{(p^ν)}(F)) is divisible by p^c, hence zero.
acceptance: For p = 2 the field F contains −1. The cocycle step needs ν ≥ N ≥ 2, not the absence of 2-power roots of unity from F that Greither states (source issue E11).

nodes.title: The real analogue of the Iwasawa–Leopoldt conjecture (Greither, Theorem 4.12 = Theorem C)
nodes.statement: Let F be a real abelian field and p a prime unramified in F, with Δ = Gal(F/ℚ) = Δ_p × Δ_0 and Δ_p cyclic. For every character χ of Δ with χ|Δ_0 ≠ ε (the order of χ is not a power of p) and χ|Δ_p faithful, |A′(F)_χ| = |½L_p(1, χ)|_p^{d(χ)}. Here A′(F) is the p-part of the projective limit of the ray class groups C_{(p^ν)}(F); A′(F) is infinite, but (1 − e_ε)A′(F) is finite.
proofSteps: Let χ′ = χ|Δ_0 ≠ 1. If Δ_p = 1, the statement is Theorem 4.11. Otherwise let C be the subgroup of Δ_p of order p, and F_1 its fixed field.
Lemma 4.13 gives α: A′(F) → A′(F_1) onto and β: A′(F_1) → A′(F) injective with βα = N_C.

If Δ_p = ⟨σ⟩ has order p^k, then N_C = Φ_{p^k}(σ), and for χ faithful on Δ_p, A′(F)_χ = A′(F)_{χ′}/Φ_{p^k}(σ)A′(F)_{χ′} (Φ_{p^k} is irreducible over the unramified ℚ_p(χ′)). Since α is onto and β injective, N_C·A′(F)_{χ′} = β(A′(F_1)_{χ′}) ≅ A′(F_1)_{χ′}, so |A′(F)_χ| = |A′(F)_{χ′}|/|A′(F_1)_{χ′}| (Solomon, Corollary II.1).

A character of F is a character of F_1 exactly when it is not faithful on Δ_p. By Theorem 4.11 the quotient is ∏|½L_p(1, ξ)|_p^{d(χ′)} over the ξ with ξ|Δ_0 = χ′ that are faithful on Δ_p. These ξ are the ℚ_p(χ′)-conjugates of χ, so the product is |½L_p(1, χ)|_p^{d(χ)}.
acceptance: χ|Δ_0 ≠ ε is needed: for Δ_p = 1 and χ = 1, A′(F)_χ has ℤ_p-rank one and L_p(s, 1) has a pole at s = 1.

nodes.title: Units modulo circular units and the Gras conjecture (Greither, Theorem 4.14 and Corollary 4.15)
nodes.statement: Let F/ℚ be real abelian with Δ = Gal(F/ℚ) = Δ_p × Δ_0 and Δ_p cyclic, and p unramified in F. Let 𝒞_F be Sinnott's group of circular units of F, E_F the unit group, C_F = 𝒞_F ∩ E_F, and (·)_p the p-adic completion. For every nontrivial character χ′ of Δ_0, |(E_F/C_F)_{p,χ′}| = |A(F)_{χ′}|·|((ℤ_p/2ℤ_p)[Δ])_{χ′}|·|(R : U)_{χ′}|, where R = ℤ[Δ] and U are as in Sinnott, and |((ℤ_p/2ℤ_p)[Δ])_{χ′}| is 2^{d(χ′)|Δ_p|} for p = 2 and 1 for odd p. If |Δ| is prime to p, then [E_{F,p}/C̄_{F,p}] = [A(F)] in the Grothendieck group K_0 of finite ℤ_p[Δ]-modules, where C̄_F is Sinnott's larger group of circular units. In particular, for p = 2 and |Δ| odd, E_F/C̄_F and A_2(F) have isomorphic composition series as ℤ_2[Δ]-modules (the Gras conjecture).
hypotheses: Sinnott's (R : U) is a generalised index of lattices, so |(R : U)_{χ′}| can be a negative power of p.
Greither prints the middle factor as 2^{d(χ′)|Δ_p|} for every p. His proof gives [e′(ℤ_p/2)[Δ]], which is 0 for odd p; the node states the corrected factor.
proofSteps: Let e′ = 1 − e_ε. The statement is equivalent to [e′(E_p/C_p)] = [e′A(F)] + [e′(ℤ_p/2)[Δ]] + [e′R/e′U] in K_0(ℤ_p[Δ]). R_{χ′} = ℤ_p(χ′)[Δ_p] is local, so the class of an R_{χ′}-module is determined by its order.

Let 𝒪 be ℤ_p with all character values adjoined. Theorem 4.11 gives [𝒪 ⊗ e′A′(F)] = Σ_χ[𝒪_χ/(½L_p(1, χ))] − [e′U_p : e′E_p] over the χ nontrivial on Δ_0. Since [E_p/C_p] = [U_p/C_p] − [U_p/E_p] and K_0(ℤ_pΔ) → K_0(𝒪Δ) is injective, it remains to prove (*) for [𝒪 ⊗ e′(U_p/C_p)].

(*) follows Sinnott §4 with p-adic L-functions: the logarithmic embedding λ: 𝒪 ⊗ U_p → p𝒪^{(Δ)}, u ↦ Σ_δ log_p(u^{δ^{−1}})·δ, gives [𝒪 ⊗ e′(U_p/C_p)] = [e′p𝒪^{(Δ)}/λ(e′C_p)], and Sinnott's Proposition 4.2 and its corollary, rewritten with L_p(1, χ), give λ(e′C_p) = e′ω′U. With R_{χ′} = ∏_χ 𝒪 the maximal order, [e′p𝒪R/e′ω′𝒪R] = [∏_χ 𝒪/(½L_p(1, χ))], and the three formulas combine to (*).

Corollary 4.15. If |Δ| is prime to p, then ℤ_pR = ℤ_pU, so [E_p/C_p] = [A(F)] + [(1 − e_ε)(ℤ_p/2)[Δ]]. For odd p that term vanishes and C̄_F/C_F is 2-elementary. For p = 2, every totally positive element of C_F is a square in E_F (Sinnott, p. 209, with (2, |Δ|) = 1), so C̄_F/C_F ≅ (1 − e_ε)(ℤ/2)[Δ], which cancels the extra term.
acceptance: For odd p the factor |((ℤ_p/2ℤ_p)[Δ])_{χ′}| is 1: both sides of 4.14 are then powers of p.

nodes.title: The odd-character form of the main conjecture at odd p
nodes.statement: Let p be odd, F_∞ = ℚ(μ_{p^∞}), Δ = Gal(ℚ(μ_p)/ℚ), Γ = Gal(F_∞/ℚ(μ_p)) and Y_∞ = lim← A_p(ℚ(μ_{p^{n+1}})), the Galois group of the maximal unramified abelian pro-p extension of F_∞. For every odd character χ ≠ ω of Δ, char_{ℤ_p(χ)[[T]]}(Y_{∞,χ}) = (G_p(T, χ̌)) with χ̌ = ωχ^{−1}, and Y_{∞,ω} has characteristic ideal (1). This is equivalent to the even form char_{Λ(Γ^+)}(X_∞^+) = I(Γ^+)ζ_p (Theorem 13.8): each follows from the other by Kummer duality between the odd part of Y_∞ and the even part of X_∞.
hypotheses: For odd p the χ-parts are exact, since p ∤ |Δ| = p − 1, and ½ is a unit, so Greither's normalisation agrees with the classical one.
proofSteps: Even to odd. This is the case F = ℚ, p odd, of L4/greither-main-conjecture-all-p. Its proof passes from the real main conjecture (here Theorem 13.8, through the four-term sequence and the local-unit theorem) to the odd components by Kummer duality (Greither, Lemma 3.3 and Proposition 3.4).

Odd to even. Kummer duality is an equality V_ρ(X^+) ≅ V_χ(Y)^*(1) of ℚ_p-representations for ρ = ωχ^{−1}. Together with μ = 0 (Ferrero–Washington) it turns the odd characteristic ideals into the even ones componentwise. The χ = ω component corresponds to the trivial component of X_∞^+, which is treated in L3/trivial-character-component.
The χ-parts match RJW's Λ(Γ^+)-module X_∞^+ through the decomposition Λ(Γ^+) = ∏_ρ ℤ_p(ρ)[[T]] over the even characters ρ of Δ, which is valid because p ∤ |Δ|.
acceptance: χ = ω is the component where Y_∞ is finite; its characteristic ideal is (1), matching the unit trivial component of I(Γ^+)ζ_p.

nodes.title: The main conjecture as Greenberg's conjecture for the Tate twists ℚ_p(n) (RJW §13.5)
nodes.statement:
Let p be odd, F = ℚ(μ_{p^∞})^+, Γ^+ = Gal(F/ℚ) and χ the cyclotomic character. For n ∈ ℤ let W_n = (ℚ_p/ℤ_p)(n), let S_n = H¹_{L_Gr}(F, W_n) be its Greenberg Selmer group, and S_n^∨ its Pontryagin dual, a finitely generated Λ(Γ^+)-module. The Greenberg condition is unramified away from p; at p it is the whole of H¹ for n ≥ 1 and the unramified subgroup for n ≤ 0. Let r_n be the order of the pole of L_∞(ℚ_p(n), s) = π^{−(s−n)/2}Γ((s−n)/2) at s = 1, and Tw_n the automorphism of Λ(Γ^+) with [g] ↦ χ(g)^n[g] (on measures, multiplication by x^n, RJW's ∂^n). Then:
(a) Greenberg's Conjecture 13.21(i) holds for every n. S_n^∨ has Λ(Γ^+)-rank r_n, which is 1 for odd n ≥ 1 and 0 otherwise.
(b) For even n ≥ 2, where r_n = r_{1−n} = 0: S_n^∨ ≅ X_∞^+(−n) and char(S_n^∨) = Tw_n(I(Γ^+)ζ_p) = Tw_n(I(Γ^+))·∂^nζ_p.
(c) For odd n ≤ −1, where r_n = r_{1−n} = 0: S_n^∨ ≅ Y_∞^{c=−1}(−n), and char(S_n^∨) is the Tw_n-twist of the odd-character characteristic ideal.
(d) For even n ≤ 0, r_{1−n} = 1, so Conjecture 13.21(ii) does not apply; this includes n = 0 (Remark 13.23).
hypotheses: Definition 13.19 asks for a G_ℚ-invariant filtration. Greenberg's condition needs only a G_{ℚ_p}-stable one; this is SelmerIwasawaCohomology/E2, and the published version prints the same text. Here V = ℚ_p(n) is one-dimensional, so nothing changes.

RJW's Example 13.22 calls Greenberg's conjecture for ℚ_p(n) 'essentially' Theorem 13.8, with p-adic L-function ∂^nζ_p. That element has a pole at the even character x^{−n} and is not in Λ(Γ^+). The integral characteristic ideal carries the factor Tw_n(I(Γ^+)), the ideal of the character x^{−n}; part (b) states the precise identity.
proofSteps: The identification of S_n. For n ≥ 1, S_n = Hom_cts((X_∞)^{c=(−1)^n}, W_n); for n ≤ 0, S_n = Hom_cts((Y_∞)^{c=(−1)^n}, W_n). Here X_∞ and Y_∞ are the Galois groups over F_∞ = ℚ(μ_{p^∞}) of the maximal abelian pro-p extensions unramified outside p and everywhere unramified, and (X_∞)^{c=1} ≅ X_∞^+ (RJW §13.5.2, requested from SelmerIwasawaCohomology L4). The Pontryagin dual of Hom_cts(M, W_n) is M(−n), with g acting as χ(g)^{−n}g. So char(M(−n)) = Tw_n(char M), since M(−n) is M pulled back along Tw_n^{−1}.

Gamma factors. The poles of Γ((s − n)/2) are at s = n − 2k, k ≥ 0, so r_n = 1 exactly when n is odd and n ≥ 1. The dual ℚ_p(n)^∨ = ℚ_p(1 − n) has r_{1−n} = 1 exactly when n is even and n ≤ 0. So (ii) applies exactly for even n ≥ 2 and odd n ≤ −1, the critical cases of Remark 13.23.

(a) X_∞^+ is torsion by Theorem 13.8, and Y_∞ is torsion. X_∞ has Λ(Γ)-rank r_2(ℚ(μ_p)) = (p − 1)/2, all of it on the c = −1 side (Iwasawa; requested from IntegralIwasawaTheory L1), which is rank one over the minus part of Λ(Γ). Twisting by an odd power of χ carries that minus part to Λ(Γ^+). So S_n^∨ has rank 1 for odd n ≥ 1 and is torsion otherwise.
(b) For even n ≥ 2, S_n^∨ = X_∞^+(−n), and Theorem 13.8 gives char = Tw_n(I(Γ^+)ζ_p) = Tw_n(I(Γ^+))·Tw_n(ζ_p). Tw_n(ζ_p) = ∂^nζ_p is RJW's twist of Kubota–Leopoldt.

(c) For odd n ≤ −1, S_n^∨ = Y_∞^{c=−1}(−n). The twist by the odd character χ^n turns Y_∞'s odd part into a Λ(Γ^+)-module, and the odd-character formulation gives its characteristic ideal componentwise.
(d) is the gamma-factor count.
acceptance: p = 3: Γ^+ = ℤ_3^×/{±1} ≅ 1 + 3ℤ_3 and X_∞^+ = 0, since the only abelian 3-ramified pro-3 extension of ℚ is the cyclotomic ℤ_3-extension. So S_n = 0 for even n ≥ 2, and char(S_n^∨) = Λ = Tw_n(I(Γ^+)ζ_3), while ∂^nζ_3 alone has a pole at x^{−n}. This separates the precise identity from the 'essentially' of Example 13.22.
n = 0 is excluded from (ii), and n = 1 has corank 1, matching r_1 = 1.

nodes.title: Norm descent for semilocal units, with bounded errors (Greither, Lemmas 2.1–2.2)
nodes.statement: Let p be a prime, F/ℚ abelian with p ∤ cond(F), K_n = F(ζ_{2p^{n+1}}) (so K_0 = F(√−1) when p = 2), K_∞ = ∪K_n, 𝒰_n = (ℤ_p ⊗ 𝒪_{K_n})^× the semilocal units above p, U_n its pro-p part, 𝒞_n Sinnott's circular units of K_n and C_n the pro-p part of their closure in 𝒰_n; 𝒰_∞, U_∞, 𝒞_∞, C_∞ the inverse limits; t = 1 for odd p and t = 2 for p = 2. (Lemma 2.2) Let H ⊆ Δ be finite abelian groups, X a ℤ_pΔ-module, X′ a ℤ_p(Δ/H)-module, and N: X → X′, i: X′ → X Δ-maps with Ni = |H| and iN = Σ_{σ∈H}σ. Then the kernel and cokernel of the induced map N̄: X_H → X′ are annihilated by |H|. (Lemma 2.1) For F′ ⊆ F with H = Gal(F/F′), the kernel and cokernel of the norm map α: (𝒰_n)_H → 𝒰′_n are annihilated by |H| = [F:F′]. (Corollary) If χ is a character of F′, the kernel and cokernel of α_χ: (𝒰_∞)_χ → (𝒰′_∞)_χ are annihilated by [F:F′]².
hypotheses: These bounds are the 'character functors and their bounded errors when the group order is divisible by p' of the stage. Since F/F′ is unramified above p, 𝒰_n is cohomologically trivial as an H-module, so α is in fact an isomorphism. The bound by |H| is all that Greither's later arguments use.
proofSteps: Lemma 2.2: if N̄(x̄) = 0, then |H|·x = iN(x) + (|H| − Σσ)x ∈ I_H·X, since Σσ ≡ |H| mod the augmentation ideal; so |H| kills ker N̄. For x′ ∈ X′, |H|x′ = N(i(x′)), so |H| kills coker N̄.
Lemma 2.1: the kernel of the norm (𝒰_n)_H → 𝒰_n^H = 𝒰′_n is a Tate cohomology group of H in degree −1, and the cokernel is Ĥ⁰(H, 𝒰_n). Both are annihilated by |H|.

Corollary: for A = ker α and B = coker α, taking χ-parts gives A_χ → 𝒰_{∞,χ} → Im(α)_χ → 0 and Tor(ℤ_p(χ), B) → Im(α)_χ → 𝒰′_{∞,χ} → B_χ → 0, with Tor over ℤ_p[Gal(F/ℚ)]. [F:F′] annihilates A_χ, B_χ and the Tor term, so the composite has kernel and cokernel killed by [F:F′]². Coinvariants commute with the inverse limit because the modules are compact.
acceptance: F′ = F: every bound is trivial.
p ∤ [F:F′]: α_χ is an isomorphism on pro-p parts.
