nodes.title: Generators of the limit of circular units (Greither, Lemma 2.3)
nodes.statement: Let p be a prime, F/ℚ abelian with p ∤ cond(F), K_n = F(ζ_{2p^{n+1}}) (so K_0 = F(√−1) when p = 2), K_∞ = ∪K_n, 𝒰_n = (ℤ_p ⊗ 𝒪_{K_n})^× the semilocal units above p, U_n its pro-p part, 𝒞_n Sinnott's circular units of K_n and C_n the pro-p part of their closure in 𝒰_n; 𝒰_∞, U_∞, 𝒞_∞, C_∞ the inverse limits; t = 1 for odd p and t = 2 for p = 2. Let m = cond(F) and G = Gal(K_∞/ℚ). For 1 ≠ m′ | m put η_{m′,F} = (N_{ℚ(m′)/ℚ(m′)∩F}(1 − ζ_{m′}^{p^{−ν}}·ζ_{p^{ν+t}}))_{ν∈ℕ}, a norm-coherent sequence. Then, up to a finite torsion group of order prime to p, 𝒞_∞ is the closure of the ℤ_pG-span of {±η_{m′,F} : 1 ≠ m′ | m} ∪ 𝒞_∞(ℚ(ζ_{p^∞})).
hypotheses: Sinnott's circular numbers D(k) = ℤ[Gal(k/ℚ)]-span{±N_{ℚ(n)/ℚ(n)∩k}(1 − ζ_n^a)} and circular units D(k) ∩ 𝒪_k^× are requested with IntegralIwasawaTheory L0 ('variants and correction factors for general abelian fields').
proofSteps: ⊇ is the definition: the η_{m′,F} are norm-coherent circular units.
Remark 1: if some relative norm of a circular number x is a unit, then x is a unit, hence a circular unit (Sinnott, p. 202).
Remark 2: in D(k) one may take a = 1, since N_{ℚ(n)/ℚ(n)∩k}(1 − ζ_n^a) is a Galois conjugate of the element for n/gcd(n, a).

Remark 3: for k of conductor dividing m, D(k) ∩ 𝒪_k[1/m]^× = ⟨±N_{ℚ(n)/ℚ(n)∩k}(1 − ζ_n) : n | m⟩. Indices n not prime to m reduce to gcd(n, m). For n prime to m, k ∩ ℚ(n) = ℚ, so those factors are integers prime to m, hence ±1.

⊆: it suffices that the universal norms in D_ν lie in A_ν, the closure of the Galois span of the η_{m′,F} at level ν and 𝒞_ν(ℚ). The key claim (**) is N_{ν+μ/ν}(D_{ν+μ}) ⊆ A′_ν·(D_ν)^{p^μ}. For x(n), n = m′p^a: when a ≤ ν + t the norm is a p^μ-th power; when a > ν + t and m′ ≠ 1, x(n) is in the Galois span of η_{m′,F}; when m′ = 1 it lies in the cyclotomic part.
Let μ → ∞, intersect with the global units (Remark 1), and pass to closures and the limit.
acceptance: F = ℚ: m = 1, so there are no η's, and 𝒞_∞ = 𝒞_∞(ℚ(ζ_{p^∞})), the cyclotomic units of ℚ(μ_{p^∞}).
The prime-to-p torsion (±1 and roots of unity of order prime to p) disappears on pro-p parts.

nodes.title: Coleman's exact sequence over unramified coefficients, including p = 2 (Greither, Theorem 2.4–Corollary 2.7)
nodes.statement: Let p be a prime, 𝒪 a finite unramified étale ℤ_p-algebra (a finite product of unramified DVRs) with Galois group Δ and primitive idempotents e_1, …, e_g, Frob its Frobenius, 𝒪[[X]]° = {f : f(0) ≡ 1 mod p}, φ: 𝒪[[X]] → 𝒪[[X]] the ℤ_p-algebra endomorphism with φ|_𝒪 = Frob and φ(1 − X) = (1 − X)^p, and Γ′ = ℤ_p^× acting by [a](1 − X) = (1 − X)^a. (Theorem 2.4) After fixing ζ = (ζ_{p^{ν+t}}) generating ℤ_p(1), for odd p there is an exact sequence of Δ × Γ′-modules 0 → ℤ_p(1)^g → 𝒪[[X]]° → 𝒪[[X]] → ℤ_p(1)^g → 0, the middle map being (1 − φ/p)∘log. For p = 2 the outer terms are (ℤ_2(1) × {±1})^g. The i-th factor maps by ζ ↦ e_i(1 − X) (and −1 ↦ −e_i for p = 2), and the last map is f ↦ ζ^{Tr(e_if′(0))}, with a second component (−1)^{Tr(e_if(0))} for p = 2. (Lemma 2.5, Theorem 2.6) With R = 𝒪[[Γ′]] and 𝒱 = ker(ψ) for Coleman's trace operator ψ: 𝒪[[X]] = R·(1 − X) + φ(𝒪[[X]]) and 𝒱 = R·(1 − X), that is, the ℤ_p[[Γ′]]-span of 𝒪·(1 − X). (Corollary 2.7) D = (1 − X)d/dX satisfies D𝒱 = 𝒱 and gives an R-isomorphism 𝒱 → 𝒱(1).
hypotheses: The input is Coleman's Division values in local fields, Theorem 2.2, for the multiplicative formal group over an unramified 𝒪_H, with torsion 𝒞 = {±1} at p = 2. Also Coleman's Local units modulo circular units, Lemma 2 and Theorem 3. These are requested from ColemanPowerSeries L1 and L3, whose coefficient extension (L0) covers unramified 𝒪; the p = 2 case is part of the request.
proofSteps: Reduce to g = 1 (𝒪 a domain) using the idempotents.
Coleman's sequence is 0 → 𝒞[+][𝒜_∞]X → ℱ(𝔪) → A → 0 with Θ_ℱ = Θ∘λ. Here λ = log (the Lubin–Tate logarithm of G_m) and Θf = f − φf/π with π = p, so Θ_ℱ = (1 − φ/p)log. ℱ(𝔪) = 𝒪[[X]]°.
𝒞 is the torsion ≡ 1 mod p: trivial for odd p and {±1} for p = 2. [𝒜_∞]X is the topological span of the (1 − X)^a, which is Γ′-isomorphic to ℤ_p(1).
A = {g : g′(0) ∈ (1 − Frob)𝒪} for odd p; for p = 2 also g(0) ∈ 2𝒪 + (1 − Frob)𝒪. Since (1 − Frob)𝒪 = ker(Tr: 𝒪 → ℤ_p), A is the kernel of the last map, which is surjective.
Lemma 2.5 and Theorem 2.6 as in Coleman's second paper, Lemma 2 and Theorem 3, using ψφ(g) = p·Frob(g) (so ψφ is injective) and ψ(1 − X) = 0.
Corollary 2.7: D(1 − X) = −(1 − X), and D([a]g) = a·[a]D(g) (chain rule), so D commutes with R up to the twist. ker D = 𝒪 and 𝒪 ∩ 𝒱 = 0 (ψ is multiplication by p on 𝒪).
acceptance: p = 2 differs only by the ±1 torsion, which appears in the first and last terms.

nodes.title: The semilocal Coleman map and its kernel and cokernel (Greither, Theorem 2.8, Lemma 2.9, Proposition 2.10)
nodes.statement: In the setting of the previous lemma, let 𝒩 be Coleman's norm operator, 𝔐 = {f ∈ 𝒪((X))^× : 𝒩f = Frob(f)} and 𝔐° = 𝔐 ∩ 𝒪[[X]]°. (Theorem 2.8) There is an exact sequence 0 → ℤ_p(1)^g → 𝔐° → 𝒱 → ℤ_p(1)^g → 0, the middle map being β = (1 − φ/p)log. (Lemma 2.9) With U_i = {x ∈ 𝒪[ζ_{p^{i+1}}] : x ≡ 1 mod (1 − ζ_{p^{i+1}})}, the map a ↦ f_a (Coleman's interpolating series, f_a(1 − ζ_{p^{i+t}}) = Frob^i(a_i)) is a ℤ_p[[Γ′]]-isomorphism U_∞ = lim U_i → 𝔐°. (Proposition 2.10) With δ = D∘log and α = Dβ = (1 − φ)δ, there are exact sequences of ℤ_p[[Γ′]][Δ]-modules 0 → ℤ_p(1)^g → 𝔐° →α 𝒱(1) → ℤ_p(1)^g → 0 and 0 → ℤ_p(1)^g → U_∞ →αψ 𝒱(1) → ℤ_p(1)^g → 0.
proofSteps: Theorem 2.8. 1 − X ∈ 𝔐 since 𝒩(1 − X) = 1 − X = Frob(1 − X). Claim: the preimage of 𝒱 under β is 𝔐° (odd p), respectively ±𝔐° (p = 2). Using ψφ = p·Frob and ψ∘log = log∘𝒩, one gets ψβ(f) = log(𝒩f/Frob f). This is 0 exactly when 𝒩f/Frob f is a root of unity ≡ 1 mod p𝒪: 1 for odd p, ±1 for p = 2, and 𝒩(−1)/Frob(−1) = −1.

The maps 𝒪[[X]] → (ℤ_p(1)[×{±1}])^g and 𝒱 → ℤ_p(1)^g have the same kernel, and the second is surjective (take y·(1 − X), y ∈ 𝒪). For p = 2 this uses that g′(0) determines g(0) mod 2 for g ∈ 𝒱, by Theorem 2.6. Combine with Theorem 2.4.
Lemma 2.9 is Coleman's Corollary 17, with Theorem 16 for the existence and uniqueness of f_a. 𝒪 may be a finite product of unramified rings.
Proposition 2.10: all maps are Δ-equivariant. The first sequence combines Corollary 2.7 with Theorem 2.8, using Dφ = pφD, so D(1 − φ/p) = (1 − φ)D. The second follows through Lemma 2.9.
acceptance: The kernel ℤ_p(1)^g is the Tate module of the roots of unity, one copy per factor of 𝒪.
The cokernel ℤ_p(1)^g is the cyclotomic moment; its ρ-part vanishes when χ(p) ≠ 1.

nodes.title: One generator per character for the circular units (Greither, Lemma 2.11 and Corollary 2.12)
nodes.statement: Let p be a prime, F/ℚ abelian with p ∤ cond(F), K_n = F(ζ_{2p^{n+1}}) (so K_0 = F(√−1) when p = 2), K_∞ = ∪K_n, 𝒰_n = (ℤ_p ⊗ 𝒪_{K_n})^× the semilocal units above p, U_n its pro-p part, 𝒞_n Sinnott's circular units of K_n and C_n the pro-p part of their closure in 𝒰_n; 𝒰_∞, U_∞, 𝒞_∞, C_∞ the inverse limits; t = 1 for odd p and t = 2 for p = 2. Let F be unramified over p, 𝒪 = ℤ_p ⊗ 𝒪_F, Δ = Gal(F/ℚ), and for a p-adic character χ of Δ and a ℤ_p[Δ]-module M let V_χ(M) = ℚ_p ⊗ M ⊗_{ℤ_p[Δ]} ℤ_p[χ]. Let χ have conductor m | cond(F) and F′ = F ∩ ℚ(m). (a) V_χ(ℚ_p ⊗_ℚ F) is generated over ℚ_pΔ by y_χ = (Tr_{ℚ(m)/F′}(ζ_m))_χ. (b) If χ ≠ 1, V_χ(C_∞) = V_χ(ℤ_p[[Γ′]][Δ])·(η_m)_χ with η_m = (N_{ℚ(m)/F′}(1 − ζ_mζ_{p^{ν+t}})^{Frob^{−ν}})_ν. (Corollary 2.12) V_χ(𝒱) is free of rank one over ℚ_p ⊗ ℤ_p(χ)[[Γ′]] on z_χ = y_χ·(1 − X).
hypotheses: Greither writes 'F′ = F ∩ ℚ(M)'. M is not defined; ℚ(m) is meant (source issue E14).
Greither's R is 𝒪[[Γ′]] on p. 460 but ℤ_p[[Γ′]] in Lemma 2.11(b), Corollary 2.12 and p. 465 (source issue E16); the node names each ring explicitly.
proofSteps: (a) ℚ_pF is generated by the x_{m′} = Tr_{ℚ(m′)/F∩ℚ(m′)}(ζ_{m′}), m′ | cond(F), by additive normal bases. ker χ acts trivially on V_χ, so ℚ_pF′ surjects onto V_χ(ℚ_pF). For a proper divisor m′ of m, pick a ≡ 1 mod m′ with χ(a) ≠ 1; then σ_a fixes x_{m′} and multiplies its image by χ(a), so the image is 0.

(b) By Lemma 2.3, C_∞ is generated by −1, the η_{m′} and the cyclotomic part C_0. Tensoring with ℚ_p, the fixed part under ker χ comes from F^{ker χ} (norm argument). As in (a) only η_m survives; C_0 dies because χ is nontrivial, and −1 dies in the pro-p part (odd p) or after ⊗ℚ_2 (p = 2).

Corollary 2.12: by (a), p^N·𝒪_χ ⊆ (ℤ_pΔ)·y_χ for some N. 𝒱 is the ℤ_p[[Γ′]]-span of 𝒪·(1 − X) (Theorem 2.6), so p^N·V_χ(𝒱) lies in the ℤ_p[[Γ′]][Δ]-span of y_χ(1 − X). That element is nonzero, and ℚ_p ⊗ ℤ_p(χ)[[Γ′]] is a PID, so V_χ(𝒱) is free on it.
acceptance: For odd p, ±1 disappears in the pro-p part; for p = 2 it disappears only after ⊗ℚ_2, which is why V_χ is used.

sources.match: Working over ℚ_p, one character at a time.

nodes.title: The Coleman image of the circular units is the Stickelberger series (Greither, Theorem 2.13 and Lemma 2.15)
nodes.statement: Let p be a prime, F/ℚ abelian with p ∤ cond(F), K_n = F(ζ_{2p^{n+1}}) (so K_0 = F(√−1) when p = 2), K_∞ = ∪K_n, 𝒰_n = (ℤ_p ⊗ 𝒪_{K_n})^× the semilocal units above p, U_n its pro-p part, 𝒞_n Sinnott's circular units of K_n and C_n the pro-p part of their closure in 𝒰_n; 𝒰_∞, U_∞, 𝒞_∞, C_∞ the inverse limits; t = 1 for odd p and t = 2 for p = 2. Let F be unramified over p, Δ = Gal(F/ℚ), Δ′ = Gal(K_0/ℚ) = Δ × Φ, Γ = Gal(K_∞/K_0), and Λ_ρ = ℤ_p(ρ)[[T]] with the involution T′ = (1 + T)^{−1} − 1. For every even nontrivial character ρ of Δ′ with χ = ωρ^{−1}: αψ(V_ρ(C_∞)) = G_p(T′, ρ)·z_{χ^{−1}} ⊂ V_ρ(𝒱(1)) = (V_{χ^{−1}}(𝒱))(1), where G_p(T, ρ) is the Stickelberger series (Washington's f(T, ρ)).
hypotheses: The statement is over ℚ_p (V_ρ). Greither expects an integral version (Remark, p. 468), which is not claimed.
Lemma 2.15(b) as printed has ζ_mζ_{p^{ν′−1}} in its second term where ζ_m^p·ζ_{p^{ν′−1}} is meant (E15). The proof's left-hand side has the correct ζ_m^p.
proofSteps: Let m = cond(ρ|Δ) and η = η_m. By Lemma 2.11(b), applied to ρ|Δ, it suffices that αψ(η_ρ) = G_p(T′, ρ)·z_{χ^{−1}} in V_{χ^{−1}}(𝒱).

Let f_0 = ζ_mX + (1 − ζ_m) and e = |(𝒪/p𝒪)^×|. Then f_0^e ≡ 1 mod p and 𝒩(f_0) = Frob(f_0), so f_0^e ∈ 𝔐°, and ψ(η^e) = N_{ℚ(m)/ℚ(m)∩F}(f_0^e). It suffices that (1 − φ)δ(f_0)_{χ^{−1}} = (G_p(T′, ρ)·ζ_m(1 − X))_{χ^{−1}}, then take the norm.

Evaluate at X = 1 − ζ_{p^{ν′}} (ν′ = ν + t); these evaluations separate points. The left side: δ(f_0) = (1 − X)ζ_m/(ζ_mX + 1 − ζ_m), so (1 − φ)δ(f_0)|_{1−ζ_{p^{ν′}}} = ζ_{p^{ν′}}ζ_m/(1 − ζ_{p^{ν′}}ζ_m) − ζ_{p^{ν′−1}}ζ_m^p/(1 − ζ_{p^{ν′−1}}ζ_m^p).

The right side: with q_ν = m·p^{ν′} and the Stickelberger elements ξ′_ν(ρ) = −q_ν^{−1}Σ_a a·ρω^{−1}(a)γ_ν(a) (Washington, p. 118), G_p(T′, ρ) = lim ξ′_ν(ρ). Then q_ν·G_p(T′, ρ)z_{χ^{−1}}|_{1−ζ_{p^{ν′}}} = −(Σ_{(a,q_ν)=1} a(ζ_mζ_{p^{ν′}})^a)_{χ^{−1}}.

Lemma 2.15: (a) Σ_{a=1}^{q_ν} a·x^a = −q_ν·x/(1 − x) for x = ζ_mζ_{p^{ν′}}, a root of unity of order q_ν, x ≠ 1. (b) Removing the multiples of p gives Σ_{(a,p)=1} a·x^a = −q_ν·x/(1 − x) + q_ν·x^p/(1 − x^p), with x^p = ζ_m^pζ_{p^{ν′−1}}. So the terms with (a, p) = 1 give the left side.
The terms with (a, m) > 1 lie in ℚ(ζ_d, ζ_{p^{ν′}}) for proper divisors d of m. Their χ^{−1}-part vanishes because m is the conductor (as in Lemma 2.11), so they contribute 0.
acceptance: m = 1 is excluded: ρ|Δ trivial would make ρ = 1 on Δ′ unless ρ is a power of ω; the trivial ρ is excluded, and V_1(U_∞/C_∞) = 0 (Greither's Remark, p. 466).
The Lemma 2.15 identities, checked numerically: (m, p, ν′) = (3, 2, 2), (5, 3, 1), (7, 2, 3), (3, 5, 1) agree to 10^{−13} with ζ_m^p in (b) and differ by 8 to 21 with the printed ζ_m.

nodes.title: Kolyvagin primes with prescribed class and Kummer symbol, including p = 2 (Greither, Theorem 3.7 and Corollary 3.8)
nodes.statement: Let K/ℚ be real abelian, G = Gal(K/ℚ), M a power of p (M ≥ 4 if p = 2), c ∈ A(K), W ⊆ K^×/K^{×M} a finite ℤ[G]-submodule and ψ: W → (ℤ/M)[G] a G-homomorphism; let 2^c be the exact power of 2 dividing cond(K). Then there are infinitely many primes λ of K such that, with ℓ the rational prime below λ and the bracketed factors present only for p = 2: (1) [λ] = [2^{c+2}]·c in A(K); (2) ℓ ≡ 1 mod M and ℓ splits completely in K; (3) (w)_ℓ = 0 in 𝒥_ℓ/M𝒥_ℓ for all w ∈ W, and there is u ∈ (ℤ/M)^× with φ_ℓ(w) = [2^{c+2}]·u·ψ(w)λ for all w ∈ W. (Complement) For K = K_ν^+ and p = 2 the factor 2^{c+2} may be replaced by 4. (Corollary 3.8) For K = K_ν^+ and every p, the conclusions hold with [λ] = p²·c and φ_ℓ(w) = p²·u·ψ(w)λ. Here 𝒥_ℓ is the group of divisors above ℓ and φ_ℓ: (𝒪_K/ℓ)^× → 𝒥_ℓ/M𝒥_ℓ is Rubin's map (Lemma 3.5).
hypotheses: For odd p this is Rubin's Theorem 3.1 (The main conjecture, appendix to Lang's Cyclotomic Fields), requested with EulerSystemsAndKolyvaginSystems ES.4 (ES.1's Chebotarev step). Lemmas 3.5 (the map φ_ℓ) and 3.6 (the Euler-system identities (κ_r)_ℓ = 0 for ℓ ∤ r and (κ_{ℓr′})_ℓ = φ_ℓ(κ_{r′})) are Rubin's Lemmas 2.3 and 2.4.
H is the 2-class field of K in the wide sense, so Gal(H/K) ≅ A(K); the Chebotarev input and the class field theory are requested (IntegralIwasawaTheory L1 and the Tau Ceti ClassFieldTheory request).
proofSteps: Claim (a): [H ∩ K′ : K] ≤ 2^c, and H ∩ K′ = K for K = K_ν^+. If c > 0, 2 ramifies in K/ℚ with exponent at most 2^{c−1}, so the primes above 2 ramify in K′/K with exponent at least M/2^c. For K = K_ν^+ the only subfield of K′ unramified everywhere over K is K.

Claim (b): Gal(H ∩ K″/K) is killed by 2^{c+1} (by 2 for K = K_ν^+). Complex conjugation j of K′ acts as −1 on Gal(K″/K′) and trivially on Gal(HK′/K′), so K″ ∩ HK′/K′ is 2-elementary; combine with (a).

Claim (c): the Kummer injection Gal(K″/K′) → Hom(W, μ_M) has cokernel killed by 2. The kernel U of K^×/K^{×M} → K′^×/K′^{×M} embeds in H¹(K′/K, μ_M). With Z = K(μ_4) ∩ K′, either Z = K and |U| ≤ 2, or U is a Klein four group bounded by |H¹(K′/Z, μ_M)|·|H¹(Z/K, μ_M)| ≤ 4.

Core: the square Gal(K″H/K) → Gal(K″/K), Gal(H/K) → Gal(K″ ∩ H/K) is cartesian, with lower right term killed by 2^{c+1}. With ι: (ℤ/M)[G] → μ_M, ι(1) = ζ_M and ι(g) = 0 for g ≠ 1, 2ιψ lifts to γ ∈ Gal(K″/K′) by (c). Choose δ ∈ Gal(K″H/K) with δ|K″ = 2^{c+1}γ and δ|H = 2^{c+1}·(c's Artin symbol). Chebotarev gives infinitely many degree-one primes λ with Frobenius δ.
δ is trivial on K′, so ℓ ≡ 1 mod M; its class on H gives (1). Comparing 'w is an M-th power mod λ' through γ and through φ_ℓ gives φ_ℓ(w) = 2^{c+2}·u·ψ(w)λ, as in Rubin, p. 403.
Complement: for K = K_ν^+, 2 replaces 2^{c+1} in the construction of δ, so the factor becomes 4. Corollary 3.8: for odd p, replace c by p²c and ψ by p²ψ in Rubin's theorem.
acceptance: p = 2 loses only a bounded power of 2 (4 at the layers K_ν^+), which the final argument absorbs.

nodes.title: Links between the Iwasawa modules and the finite layers, with bounded constants (Greither, Lemmas 3.9–3.11)
nodes.statement: Let F/ℚ be abelian and unramified at p, K_n = F(ζ_{2p^{n+1}}), Δ = Gal(K_0^+/ℚ), G_n = Gal(K_n^+/ℚ), Γ_n = Gal(K_n^+/K_0^+), γ a generator of Γ = lim Γ_n and γ_n = γ^{p^n}. Write X = lim A(K_n^+), and E_∞, C_∞ for the plus-part limits of the global units and circular units. For an even character χ ≠ 1 of Δ put Λ_χ = ℤ_p(χ)[[T]], Λ_{n,χ} = Λ_χ/(1 − γ_n), and let H_χ generate char((E_∞/C_∞)_χ). Fix a quasi-isomorphism X_χ → ⊕_{i=1}^k Λ_χ/(g_i), so that char(X_χ) = (g) with g = g_1⋯g_k. (Lemma 3.9) There are c_1 = c_1(F) and G_n-maps ϑ_n: E_{n,χ} → Λ_{n,χ} with (γ − 1)²p^{c_1}·H_χ·Λ_{n,χ} ⊆ ϑ_n(im C_{n,χ}) ⊆ p^{−c_1}·H_χ·Λ_{n,χ}. (Lemma 3.10) There are c_2 = c_2(F) and G_n-maps τ_n: A_{n,χ} → ⊕_i Λ_{n,χ}/(g_i) with p^{c_2}·coker(τ_n) = 0. (Lemma 3.11) γ − 1 acts on X with finite kernel and cokernel.
hypotheses: Rubin's Lemma 1.2 (Invent. Math. 93 (1988)) bounds (γ − 1)Ĥ^i(Γ_{mn}, E_m) for i ∈ {−1, 0} uniformly. Greither notes that its hypothesis '[K_0^+ : ℚ] prime to p' is not used in full: it suffices that the primes above p are totally ramified in K_∞^+/K_0^+ and that K_0^+ is linearly disjoint from the cyclotomic ℤ_p-extension of ℚ. Requested with IntegralIwasawaTheory L2.
proofSteps: Lemma 3.9. The sequence 0 → lim H^{−1}(Γ_{mn}, E_m) → (E_∞)_{1−γ_n} → E_n → lim H⁰(Γ_{mn}, E_m) → 0 has outer terms killed by (γ − 1)p^κ.
V_χ(U_∞) is free cyclic over ℚ_p ⊗ Λ_χ (proof of Corollary 2.14), hence so is V_χ(E_∞). This gives α: E_{∞,χ} → Λ_χ with finite cokernel and kernel killed by a power of p.
A Tor argument gives 0 → A_n → (E_{∞,χ})_{1−γ_n} → E_{n,χ} → B_n → 0 with (γ − 1)p^{c′} killing A_n and B_n. Maps ϑ_n then fit a square with (γ − 1)²p^{2c′}α on top (Rubin, p. 705).

H_χ·(α(E_{∞,χ})/α(im C_{∞,χ})) is finite, so p^sH_χ ∈ α(im C_{∞,χ}), giving (γ − 1)²p^{s+2c′}H_χΛ_{n,χ} ⊆ ϑ_n(im C_{n,χ}). Also p^{s′}·im C_{∞,χ} ⊆ H_χE_{∞,χ}, because ℚ_pE_{∞,χ} is cyclic. Take c_1 = max(s′, s + 2c′).

Lemma 3.11. X is finitely generated Λ-torsion, so it suffices that Z = X/(γ − 1)X is finite. Z is the Galois group of the maximal unramified p-extension N of K_∞^+ that is abelian over K_0^+. N is unramified outside p and is a compositum of finitely many ℤ_p-extensions and a finite extension. By Leopoldt for the real abelian K_0^+ its only ℤ_p-extension is K_∞^+, so N/K_∞^+ is finite.

Lemma 3.10. By Washington, p. 278, A_n ≅ X/Y_n with Y_n = ((1 − γ_n)/(1 − γ))·Y_0 and (γ − 1)X ⊆ Y_0 ⊆ X. So the kernel of X/(1 − γ_n)X → A_n is a quotient of Y_0/(γ − 1)X, which is finite by 3.11. The kernels are bounded, the same holds on χ-parts (Tor), and τ_n comes from the quasi-isomorphism.
acceptance: The constants c_1, c_2 depend on F only, not on n; this is what the induction needs.

nodes.title: The Kolyvagin step and the Maschke lift (Greither, Lemmas 3.12–3.13)
nodes.statement: (Lemma 3.12) Let K/ℚ be real abelian, G = Gal(K/ℚ), Δ ⊆ G, χ a character of Δ, M a power of p, r = ℓ_1⋯ℓ_ν ∈ 𝒮_{M,K}, ℓ = ℓ_ν, λ a prime of K above ℓ, and c = [λ] ∈ A = A(K). Let B ⊆ A be generated by the classes of the primes above ℓ_1, …, ℓ_{ν−1}. Let x ∈ K^×/K^{×M} with (x)_{[q]} = 0 for every prime q ∤ r, and W its ℤ_p[G]-span. Suppose E, g, η ∈ ℤ_p[G] satisfy (i) E·Ann((c)_χ ∈ (A/B)_χ) ⊆ g·(ℤ_p[G])_χ; (ii) (ℤ_p[G])_χ/(g) is finite; (iii) M ≥ |A_χ|·|η·((𝒥_ℓ/M𝒥_ℓ)/(W)_{[ℓ]})_χ|. Then there is a G-homomorphism ψ: W_χ → (ℤ/M)[G]_χ with (g·ψ(x)λ)_χ = E·η·(x_{[ℓ]})_χ. (Lemma 3.13) For a ℤ_p[Δ]-module N and π: N → N_χ the projection, there is a ℤ_p[Δ]-map ε_χ: N_χ → N with π∘ε_χ = |Δ|·id.
proofSteps: Lemma 3.12. Choose a lift β of x and write (β)_{[ℓ]} = v_λ(β)λ, where ℓ splits totally in K. Since M·A_χ = 0 by (iii), the image of (β)_{[ℓ]} in (A/B)_χ is that of the principal ideal (β), hence trivial. So v_λ(β) kills (c)_χ, and by (i) E·v_λ(β)_χ = g·δ in R = (ℤ_p[G])_χ.
Division by g is unique in R, which has no ℤ_p-torsion and R/(g) finite by (ii). Define ψ(ρx) = ηρδ mod MR. Then g·ψ(x)λ = η·E·v_λ(β) = E·η·(x)_{[ℓ]}.

Well-definedness: if ρx = 0, then ρβ = y^M. By (iii) and h = |A_χ|, ηρ kills M·h^{−1}(𝒥_ℓ/M𝒥_ℓ)_χ ≅ R/hR, so h | ηρ in R/MR. Writing (y) over the primes q, multiplying by η and passing to (A/B)_χ shows that η·v_λ(y) kills c_χ. By (i), E·η·v_λ(y)_χ ∈ gR, hence E·η·v_λ(ρx) ∈ MgR, and ηρδ ∈ MR.
Lemma 3.13 (Maschke): reduce to N = ℤ_p[Δ], N_χ = ℤ_p(χ); with f a ℤ_p-linear section of π, ε_χ(y) = Σ_{δ∈Δ} δf(δ^{−1}y).
acceptance: The factor |Δ| from 3.13 and the factors p² from Corollary 3.8 are what the induction accumulates.
